deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.2 端緒 — Vocabulary
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第二章「端緒」
notes: Harder vocabulary (N2–N1, literary narration, story terms) for Chapter 2. Chapter 2 starts on p.9. Cards from pp.9 and 12–21 are checked against the printed pages and come first, in page order (pp.10–11 weren't photographed; their cards are marked). Cards after that are built from the chapter's scenes and the novel's style and say 'Not yet checked' in their scene — some of them may turn out to belong to Chapter 3. Example sentences are original, not quoted from the book.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

cards.scene: The heading on p.9: 第二章「端緒」. The chapter opens with 瀧's dream and his first morning in 三葉's body.
cards.context: 端 (edge, end) + 緒 (the end of a thread or cord, as in へその緒): the loose end you can pull to unravel something — fitting for a story about braided cords. Also read たんちょ. Typical use: 事件の端緒をつかむ 'get the first lead in a case'.
cards.example_sentence: 小さな違和感が、すべての謎を解く端緒になった。
cards.example_reading: ちいさな いわかん が、 すべて の なぞ を とく たんしょ に なった。
cards.example_meaning: A small feeling that something was off became the first clue to solving the whole mystery.

cards.scene: p.9 — a lonely voice, trembling like a distant star.
cards.context: 震 (quake) — the same kanji as 地震. 手が震える, 声が震える (voice trembles), 寒さに震える. Transitive: 震わせる (肩を震わせて泣く = cry with shaking shoulders).
cards.example_sentence: 緊張で、発表のあいだずっと声が震えていた。
cards.example_reading: きんちょう で、 はっぴょう の あいだ ずっと こえ が ふるえて いた。
cards.example_meaning: My voice trembled with nerves through the whole presentation.

cards.scene: p.9 — someone is calling his name (名を呼ばれている). The book's title 君の名は。 uses the same 名.
cards.context: 名 on its own, read な, is the literary/older word for 名前: 名を名乗る (to give one's name), 名もない花 (a nameless flower), 名が知れる (to become well known). In compounds it is usually めい/みょう (有名, 名字), so the bare な reading is worth drilling.
cards.example_sentence: 名も知らない人のことを、どうしてこんなに思い出すのだろう。
cards.example_reading: な も しらない ひと の こと を、 どうして こんなに おもいだす の だろう。
cards.example_meaning: Why do I keep thinking about someone whose name I don't even know?

cards.scene: p.9 — he suddenly realises he's on a packed train.
cards.context: 満員 = full to capacity (満 full + 員 members); 満員御礼 = 'sold out, thank you'. 満員電車 is the fixed phrase for rush-hour trains. Compare 満席 (all seats taken).
cards.example_sentence: 毎朝の満員電車で、もう疲れてしまう。
cards.example_reading: まいあさ の まんいん でんしゃ で、 もう つかれて しまう。
cards.example_meaning: The packed train every morning wears me out before the day even starts.

cards.scene: p.9 — 瀧 hears the strange bell from inside a half-asleep doze; on p.14 that doze finally lifts and he's fully awake.
cards.context: Noun from まどろむ (to doze lightly). A soft, literary word; in speech you'd say うとうとする. まどろみの中で = while half-asleep. The kanji 微睡み is rare, so books usually write it in kana.
cards.example_sentence: 日曜の朝、まどろみの中で雨の音を聞いていた。
cards.example_reading: にちよう の あさ、 まどろみ の なか で あめ の おと を きいて いた。
cards.example_meaning: On Sunday morning I lay half-asleep, listening to the rain.

cards.scene: p.9 — the girl calling 瀧's name sounds close to tears, her voice earnest and desperate.
cards.context: 切 (cut, acute) + 実 (real): something felt so sharply it hits you directly. 切実な声 / 切実な願い (a heartfelt wish) / 切実な問題 (a pressing problem) / 切実に感じる (to feel keenly). Stronger and more personal than 真剣 (serious).
cards.example_sentence: 電話の向こうから、助けを求める切実な声が聞こえた。
cards.example_reading: でんわ の むこう から、 たすけ を もとめる せつじつな こえ が きこえた。
cards.example_meaning: From the other end of the line came a desperate voice asking for help.

cards.scene: p.9 — 瀧 hears the girl's voice as something like the twinkle of a distant star: faint, fragile and lonely.
cards.context: The same kanji also reads まばたき (blinking your eyes, the everyday word). またたき is the literary reading, used mostly for stars and lights; verb 瞬く (またたく). 瞬く間に = in the blink of an eye. 瞬間 (しゅんかん, moment) uses the same kanji.
cards.example_sentence: 山の上では、星の瞬きがはっきり見える。
cards.example_reading: やま の うえ では、 ほし の またたき が はっきり みえる。
cards.example_meaning: Up in the mountains you can clearly see the stars twinkling.

cards.scene: p.9 — the girl's voice anxiously asks 瀧 if he remembers her; on p.12 he points at himself and asks the little girl a question.
cards.context: Written-register 'ask': narration uses 問う where speech would say 聞く or 尋ねる. Also 'call into question': 責任を問う (hold someone responsible), 年齢を問わず (regardless of age). Its て/た forms are 問うて / 問うた, not 問って.
cards.example_sentence: 祖母は静かに「本当に後悔しないの？」と問うた。
cards.example_reading: そぼ は しずかに 「ほんとうに こうかい しない の？」 と とうた。
cards.example_meaning: Grandmother asked quietly, "Are you sure you won't regret it?"

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — 瀧 wakes up — but in a room, and a body, that are not his.
cards.context: More literary than 目が覚める or 起きる, so narration likes it. Also figurative: 才能に目覚める 'discover a talent'. Noun 目覚め; 目覚まし時計 = alarm clock.
cards.example_sentence: 目覚めると、窓の外で鳥が鳴いていた。
cards.example_reading: めざめる と、 まど の そと で とり が ないて いた。
cards.example_meaning: When I woke, birds were singing outside the window.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — 瀧 opens his eyes in an unfamiliar room in a mountain town he has never seen.
cards.context: An old negative form (ぬ = ない) that only goes before nouns: 見知らぬ人 'a stranger', 見知らぬ町. Written/literary — in speech you'd say 知らない. Compare 見慣れない 'not used to seeing'.
cards.example_sentence: 見知らぬ人に道を聞かれて、少し驚いた。
cards.example_reading: みしらぬ ひと に みち を きかれて、 すこし おどろいた。
cards.example_meaning: I was a little surprised when a stranger asked me for directions.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — Everything feels wrong to 瀧 — the weight of the body, the long hair, the voice.
cards.context: 違 (differ) + 和 (harmony) + 感 (feeling): something doesn't fit. 違和感がある / 違和感を覚える. Also physical: 目に違和感がある 'my eye feels funny'. A key mood word for the whole swap story.
cards.example_sentence: 新しい眼鏡をかけたら、しばらく違和感があった。
cards.example_reading: あたらしい めがね を かけたら、 しばらく いわかん が あった。
cards.example_meaning: When I put on my new glasses, they felt strange for a while.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — 瀧 has no idea where he is or what to do, and the morning carries on around him anyway.
cards.context: Lit. 'to be lost at the door' (戸 + 惑う). Used when you don't know how to react to something new: 急な変化に戸惑う. Noun 戸惑い. Softer, more about uncertainty than 混乱 (total confusion).
cards.example_sentence: 初めての町で、バスの乗り方に戸惑った。
cards.example_reading: はじめて の まち で、 バス の のりかた に とまどった。
cards.example_meaning: In an unfamiliar town, I wasn't sure how to ride the bus.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — 瀧 stares hard at an unfamiliar girl's face in the mirror.
cards.context: Almost always まじまじと見る / 見つめる — staring because you can't believe what you see. Different from じろじろ (rude staring at others) and じっと (holding still and watching). Unrelated to the slang マジ.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は写真の中の自分をまじまじと見つめた。
cards.example_reading: かれ は しゃしん の なか の じぶん を まじまじと みつめた。
cards.example_meaning: He stared hard at himself in the photo.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — The arms and fingers 瀧 looks down at are thin and delicate — nothing like his own.
cards.context: Irregular reading: 華 is normally か/はな and 奢 is normally しゃ/おごる. Used for slim, fragile-looking bodies or objects: 華奢な肩, 華奢なネックレス. Often written きゃしゃ.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は華奢に見えるが、実はとても力が強い。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は きゃしゃ に みえる が、 じつ は とても ちから が つよい。
cards.example_meaning: She looks delicate, but she's actually very strong.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — The famous comic beat — 瀧, sure it's a dream, checks 'his' new chest, which is not what a little sister wants to see at breakfast time.
cards.context: Basic sense: knead or squeeze with the hands — 肩を揉む 'massage someone's shoulders'. Idiom: 気を揉む 'to fret' (lit. knead one's spirit). 揉 is outside the common-use kanji list, so it is often written もむ.
cards.example_sentence: 疲れている母の肩を揉んであげた。
cards.example_reading: つかれて いる はは の かた を もんで あげた。
cards.example_meaning: I massaged my tired mother's shoulders.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — The 'dream' feels far too real — the air, the floor, the body all register vividly.
cards.context: 生 (raw, alive) doubled: so fresh it still feels alive. 生々しい記憶, 生々しい傷. Often has a slightly unpleasant 'too real' edge, unlike the neutral 鮮やか (bright, vivid).
cards.example_sentence: 事故の記憶は、今でも生々しく残っている。
cards.example_reading: じこ の きおく は、 いま でも なまなましく のこって いる。
cards.example_meaning: The memory of the accident is still raw and vivid.

cards.scene: pp.10–11 (not photographed yet) — For a dream, everything feels oddly detailed — a feeling both heroes keep returning to.
cards.context: 妙 = strange, peculiar (妙な夢 'a weird dream'), but also 'exquisite' in 絶妙 (perfect timing/balance). 妙に静かだ, 妙に落ち着く — something is off but you can't say why. Narration loves it.
cards.example_sentence: 今日の教室は妙に静かだった。
cards.example_reading: きょう の きょうしつ は みょうに しずか だった。
cards.example_meaning: The classroom was strangely quiet today.

cards.scene: p.12 — 四葉: are you still half asleep? (寝ぼけとんの？)
cards.context: 寝ぼけて〜 = did something while half-awake. 寝ぼけてるの？ is the natural teasing 'Are you still asleep?' for someone acting oddly in the morning. 寝ぼけ眼 (ねぼけまなこ) = sleepy eyes.
cards.example_sentence: 寝ぼけて、弟の靴をはいて家を出てしまった。
cards.example_reading: ねぼけて、 おとうと の くつ を はいて いえ を でて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: Half-asleep, I left the house wearing my little brother's shoes.

cards.simpler_synonym: びっくりして何も言えない
cards.scene: p.12 — 四葉 looks utterly fed up with him (呆れきった); on p.19 サヤちん is too.
cards.context: Disbelief mixed with disgust or exasperation: 呆れた顔, 呆れて物も言えない 'so appalled I'm speechless'. Not plain surprise — there's always a judgment in it. Often written あきれる.
cards.example_sentence: 弟がまた宿題を忘れたと聞いて、母は呆れていた。
cards.example_reading: おとうと が また しゅくだい を わすれた と きいて、 はは は あきれて いた。
cards.example_meaning: Mother was exasperated to hear my little brother had forgotten his homework again.

cards.scene: p.12 — the dressing table at the edge of his vision.
cards.context: 視 (look) + 界 (boundary, world). 視界がぼやける / にじむ (vision blurs), 視界に入る (come into view), 視界が悪い (poor visibility, e.g. in fog).
cards.example_sentence: 霧で視界が悪く、車はゆっくり進んだ。
cards.example_reading: きり で しかい が わるく、 くるま は ゆっくり すすんだ。
cards.example_meaning: Visibility was poor in the fog, so the cars moved slowly.

meanings: eyes slanting up at the outer corners
cards.scene: p.12 — 四葉 has twin tails and rather upturned eyes (ツリ目がち), the look of a feisty kid.
cards.context: From 吊る (つる, to hang or pull up): eyes whose outer corners lift, a classic sign of a strong-willed character in comics. Opposite: タレ目 (droopy eyes). 〜がち = tending to, so ツリ目がち = with rather upturned eyes. Also written つり目 / 吊り目.
cards.example_sentence: 妹はツリ目なので、普通にしていても怒っているとよく誤解される。
cards.example_reading: いもうと は つりめ なので、 ふつう に して いて も おこって いる と よく ごかい される。
cards.example_meaning: My little sister has upturned eyes, so people often think she's angry even when she isn't.

cards.scene: p.12 — 四葉 scolds her 'sister' for being half-asleep and slams the sliding door shut.
cards.context: 叩く (to hit) + つける (onto): to bang or hurl something down with force. 机に本を叩きつける, 地面に叩きつけられる, 雨が窓に叩きつける (rain lashes the window). 叩きつけるように閉める = to shut as if hurling it, i.e. to slam.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は怒って、スマホを机に叩きつけた。
cards.example_reading: かれ は おこって、 スマホ を つくえ に たたきつけた。
cards.example_meaning: He got angry and slammed his phone down on the desk.

cards.scene: p.12 — after the door slams, 瀧 thinks what a violent little girl that was.
cards.context: 凶 (evil, bad luck, as in 大凶 on an おみくじ) + 暴 (violent, as in 暴力). Normally used for dangerous animals or criminals (凶暴な犬, 凶暴な性格), so using it for a ten-year-old is comic exaggeration. Also written 狂暴. 乱暴 is the everyday word for rough behaviour.
cards.example_sentence: このクマは凶暴なので、近づかないでください。
cards.example_reading: この クマ は きょうぼう なので、 ちかづかないで ください。
cards.example_meaning: This bear is dangerous, so please don't go near it.

cards.scene: p.12 — 瀧 privately labels 四葉 a 'violent female child', using a stiff official word as a joke.
cards.context: Formal word from news reports, police, medical and legal language (女児が保護された), and toy marketing (女児向け = for girls). Boy: 男児. 瀧 thinking of 四葉 as a 女児 is deadpan humour, like calling her 'a female minor'.
cards.example_sentence: 公園で迷子になっていた五歳の女児が、無事に保護された。
cards.example_reading: こうえん で まいご に なって いた ごさい の じょじ が、 ぶじ に ほご された。
cards.example_meaning: A five-year-old girl who had got lost in the park was found safe.

cards.scene: p.12 — 四葉 opens the sliding door to the room, then slams it shut again.
cards.context: Thick, opaque, paper-covered sliding door between rooms in a Japanese house, unlike 障子 (しょうじ), the translucent screens that let light through. 襖を開ける / 閉める; closet (押し入れ) doors are also 襖. The kanji is rare, so learn it as ふすま.
cards.example_sentence: 隣の部屋から、襖ごしに笑い声が聞こえてきた。
cards.example_reading: となり の へや から、 ふすま ごし に わらいごえ が きこえて きた。
cards.example_meaning: Laughter came through the sliding door from the next room.

cards.scene: p.12 — 瀧 notices a dressing table with a mirror, which leads to the mirror scene on p.13.
cards.context: 鏡 (mirror; read きょう in compounds) + 台 (stand). A low traditional dressing table you sit at on the floor; a Western one is a ドレッサー. Careful: 兄弟 (siblings) is also きょうだい.
cards.example_sentence: 祖母の部屋には、古い木の鏡台がある。
cards.example_reading: そぼ の へや に は、 ふるい き の きょうだい が ある。
cards.example_meaning: There's an old wooden dressing table in my grandmother's room.

cards.scene: p.12 — 瀧's eyes land on the dressing table in the corner of the room.
cards.context: Also written 目が留まる. 目がとまる = your gaze stops on something; 目に留まる = something catches the eye of a person (社長の目に留まる = get noticed by the boss); 目を留める = to fix your eyes on it on purpose.
cards.example_sentence: 本屋で、きれいな表紙の本に目がとまった。
cards.example_reading: ほんや で、 きれいな ひょうし の ほん に め が とまった。
cards.example_meaning: In the bookshop, a book with a beautiful cover caught my eye.

cards.scene: p.13 — long black hair with bedhead sticking up here and there.
cards.context: 寝 (sleep) + 癖 (habit; a kink or curl). 寝癖がつく = to get bedhead; 寝癖を直す = to fix it. 癖 alone (くせ) = a habit: 口癖 (くちぐせ) = a pet phrase.
cards.example_sentence: 寝癖がひどくて、帽子をかぶって学校に行った。
cards.example_reading: ねぐせ が ひどくて、 ぼうし を かぶって がっこう に いった。
cards.example_meaning: My bedhead was so bad I wore a hat to school.

cards.scene: p.13 — in the mirror (the book writes it in kana: ふくらみ).
cards.context: Noun from 膨らむ 'to swell' (パンが膨らむ, 夢が膨らむ 'a dream grows'). 胸の膨らみ is the polite, literary way prose refers to breasts. 膨 is a hard kanji — anchor the reading with ふくらむ.
cards.example_sentence: つぼみの膨らみに、春が近いことを感じた。
cards.example_reading: つぼみ の ふくらみ に、 はる が ちかい こと を かんじた。
cards.example_meaning: In the swelling of the buds, I felt that spring was near.

cards.scene: p.13 — the hair in the mirror sticks up in tufts, messed up by bedhead (寝癖).
cards.context: 飛ぶ (fly) + 跳ねる (bounce, spring): to leap or hop about. うれしくて飛び跳ねる (jump for joy), 魚が飛び跳ねる. For hair, 跳ねる means strands sticking out: 髪が跳ねている = my hair's sticking up.
cards.example_sentence: 合格の知らせを聞いて、妹は飛び跳ねて喜んだ。
cards.example_reading: ごうかく の しらせ を きいて、 いもうと は とびはねて よろこんだ。
cards.example_meaning: When she heard she'd passed, my little sister jumped for joy.

cards.scene: p.13 — in the mirror: a small, round face.
cards.context: 丸 (round) + 顔, with 顔 voiced to がお: same pattern as 笑顔 (えがお), 横顔 (よこがお, profile), 寝顔 (ねがお, sleeping face). The contrast is 面長 (おもなが, a long face).
cards.example_sentence: 姉は丸顔なので、年より若く見られる。
cards.example_reading: あね は まるがお なので、 とし より わかく みられる。
cards.example_meaning: My older sister has a round face, so people think she's younger than she is.

cards.scene: p.13 — big eyes in the mirror that look as if they want to ask something (もの問いたげ).
cards.context: Literally the pupil, but in writing it's a poetic word for the eyes themselves: 大きな瞳, 澄んだ瞳 (clear eyes). Speech uses 目. Also a common girl's name. もの問いたげ = looking as if wanting to ask, echoing 問う from p.9 (〜たげ = seeming to want to).
cards.example_sentence: その子は大きな瞳で、じっと私を見つめていた。
cards.example_reading: その こ は おおきな ひとみ で、 じっと わたし を みつめて いた。
cards.example_meaning: The child was gazing steadily at me with big eyes.

cards.scene: p.13 — 瀧 notes the slim neck and deep collarbones in the mirror.
cards.context: 鎖 (chain, くさり) + 骨 (bone, こつ in compounds, as in 骨折 こっせつ = fracture and 肋骨 later on this page). An anatomy word, but common when describing a slender figure: 深い鎖骨 = deep, prominent collarbones.
cards.example_sentence: 自転車で転んで、鎖骨を折ってしまった。
cards.example_reading: じてんしゃ で ころんで、 さこつ を おって しまった。
cards.example_meaning: I fell off my bike and broke my collarbone.

cards.scene: p.13 — the chest seems to be insisting on how healthily it has grown, in 瀧's tongue-in-cheek narration.
cards.context: 主張する = to insist, assert or claim (an opinion, a right): 自分の意見を主張する, 無実を主張する (claim innocence). The book uses it humorously for a body, with 〜かのような (as if). Things that stand out can 'assert' themselves too: 主張の強い色 (a loud colour).
cards.example_sentence: 彼は最後まで、自分は悪くないと主張した。
cards.example_reading: かれ は さいご まで、 じぶん は わるく ない と しゅちょう した。
cards.example_meaning: He insisted to the end that he hadn't done anything wrong.

cards.scene: p.13 — the shadows of the ribs show faintly (うっすらと浮かぶ).
cards.context: Mimetic adverb from 薄い (thin, faint), often with と. うっすら雪が積もる (a light dusting of snow), うっすら涙を浮かべる (eyes slightly wet), うっすら覚えている (vaguely remember).
cards.example_sentence: 朝起きると、庭にうっすらと雪が積もっていた。
cards.example_reading: あさ おきる と、 にわ に うっすら と ゆき が つもって いた。
cards.example_meaning: When I got up in the morning, there was a light dusting of snow in the garden.

cards.scene: p.13 — the shadows of the ribs are faintly visible in the mirror.
cards.context: 肋 (rib, ろく) + 骨 (こつ) with a sound change: ろく + こつ → ろっこつ. The everyday spoken word is あばら / あばら骨. Like 鎖骨 above, anatomy words with 骨 usually read it こつ.
cards.example_sentence: サッカーの試合中にぶつかって、肋骨にひびが入った。
cards.example_reading: サッカー の しあい ちゅう に ぶつかって、 ろっこつ に ひび が はいった。
cards.example_meaning: I collided with someone during a football match and cracked a rib.

cards.scene: p.13 — the soft curve of the waist completes 瀧's survey of the body in the mirror.
cards.context: 曲 (bend) + 線 (line); the opposite is 直線 (ちょくせん, straight line). Used for graphs, design and the lines of a body (体の曲線). カーブ is the everyday loanword, especially for roads.
cards.example_sentence: この橋は、美しい曲線を描いている。
cards.example_reading: この はし は、 うつくしい きょくせん を えがいて いる。
cards.example_meaning: This bridge traces a beautiful curve.

cards.scene: p.13 — 瀧 admits he's never actually seen a girl's body in person.
cards.context: 生 (なま) = raw, but 生で also means 'live, in the flesh', as opposed to on a screen or in pictures: 生で見る, 生で聞く. Same idea in 生放送 (live broadcast) and 生ビール (draught beer). Conversational in tone.
cards.example_sentence: 好きな歌手の歌を、初めて生で聞いた。
cards.example_reading: すきな かしゅ の うた を、 はじめて なま で きいた。
cards.example_meaning: I heard my favourite singer live for the first time.

cards.scene: p.13 — the pajamas slip off and drop softly to the floor.
cards.context: The sound of something light and dry (cloth, paper, hair) falling, usually ぱさり(と)落ちる. Variants: ぱさっ; ばさっ is heavier and louder. Related ぱさぱさ = dry and crumbly (dry hair, dry bread).
cards.example_sentence: 本の間から、古い手紙がぱさりと床に落ちた。
cards.example_reading: ほん の あいだ から、 ふるい てがみ が ぱさり と ゆか に おちた。
cards.example_meaning: An old letter slipped out from between the pages and dropped softly to the floor.

cards.scene: p.14 — his head clears all at once, and he panics all at once.
cards.context: 混乱する 'to be confused / thrown into chaos'; 頭が混乱する 'my head is spinning'. Works for people and for situations (交通が混乱する 'traffic is in chaos'). Stronger than 戸惑う.
cards.example_sentence: 急にいろいろなことを言われて、頭が混乱した。
cards.example_reading: きゅう に いろいろ な こと を いわれて、 あたま が こんらん した。
cards.example_meaning: I was told so many things at once that my head was spinning.

cards.scene: p.14 — The sleepy haze that had been wrapped around the body 瀧 woke up in finally lifts.
cards.context: To cover something over completely: 雲が空を覆う (clouds cover the sky), 顔を手で覆う (cover your face with your hands). Here it's figurative — drowsiness (まどろみ, a light doze) lies over his whole body like a blanket. More literary than かぶせる or 包む; the passive 覆われる is very common.
cards.example_sentence: 朝起きると、町は一面の霧に覆われていた。
cards.example_reading: あさ おきる と、 まち は いちめん の きり に おおわれて いた。
cards.example_meaning: When I woke up, the whole town was covered in fog.

meanings: (of the sky) to be clear all over
cards.scene: p.14 — The haze in 瀧's head clears completely and he is suddenly wide awake.
cards.context: In kanji 晴れ渡る: 晴れる (to clear) + 渡る (across) → clear from edge to edge, normally said of the sky (晴れわたった青空). 新海誠 uses it for the mind: the fog of sleep clears away. Same 'all across' 〜わたる as 澄みわたる (to be crystal clear all over) and 響きわたる (to ring out everywhere).
cards.example_sentence: 週末は空が晴れわたって、遠くの山まではっきり見えた。
cards.example_reading: しゅうまつ は そら が はれわたって、 とおく の やま まで はっきり みえた。
cards.example_meaning: At the weekend the sky cleared completely and you could see right to the distant mountains.

meanings: unable to bear it any longer
cards.scene: p.14 — It sinks in that he's in a girl's body, and 瀧 can't take it any more: he screams.
cards.context: From たまる (堪る, to endure) + the classical negative ず: 'not enduring' → can't hold it in. Usually followed by an action: たまらず笑い出す, たまらず逃げ出す; the book adds に (たまらずに). Related everyday adjective: たまらない = unbearable / irresistible (暑くてたまらない).
cards.example_sentence: あまりの寒さに、たまらず店の中に逃げこんだ。
cards.example_reading: あまり の さむさ に、 たまらず みせ の なか に にげこんだ。
cards.example_meaning: It was so cold that I couldn't stand it and ducked into a shop.

cards.scene: p.14 — After the scene break 三葉 is narrating: she slides open the door into the living room.
cards.context: 引く (to pull, slide) + 戸 (door). Traditional Japanese houses are full of sliding doors; a hinged door is 開き戸 (ひらきど) or ドア. Paper-covered ones have their own names: 襖 (ふすま) and 障子 (しょうじ). You still use 開ける / 閉める with them.
cards.example_sentence: 古い旅館の引き戸は、開けるたびにがたがたと音がした。
cards.example_reading: ふるい りょかん の ひきど は、 あける たび に がたがた と おと が した。
cards.example_meaning: The sliding door at the old inn rattled every time you opened it.

cards.scene: p.14 — The moment 三葉 walks in, 四葉 snaps at her in an aggressive tone for being late.
cards.context: 攻撃 (attack) + 的 (-ive). な-adjective: 攻撃的な態度 (hostile attitude), 攻撃的な性格. Here it's playful exaggeration — a ten-year-old's whiny 'you're late!' described as if it were an assault.
cards.example_sentence: 疲れているときは、つい攻撃的な言い方をしてしまう。
cards.example_reading: つかれて いる とき は、 つい こうげきてきな いいかた を して しまう。
cards.example_meaning: When I'm tired, I tend to say things in an aggressive way.

cards.scene: p.14 — 四葉's sharp tone of voice comes flying at 三葉 as she opens the door.
cards.context: Irregular reading: こわ- is an old combining form of こえ (as in 声高 こわだか, loudly). 声色 is the colour or tone of a voice, or an imitation of someone's voice (声色を使う = to put on someone's voice). The book has 声色が飛んできた — the voice 'flew in' at her.
cards.example_sentence: 母の声色で、怒っているのがすぐに分かった。
cards.example_reading: はは の こわいろ で、 おこって いる の が すぐ に わかった。
cards.example_meaning: I could tell at once from Mum's tone of voice that she was angry.

cards.scene: p.14 — 三葉 grumbles that 四葉 hasn't even lost all her baby teeth yet.
cards.context: 乳 (milk) + 歯 (tooth); adult teeth are 永久歯 (えいきゅうし). 三葉 uses it as a put-down: you're still a little kid, so don't act superior.
cards.example_sentence: 弟は、ぐらぐらしていた乳歯がやっと抜けて喜んでいる。
cards.example_reading: おとうと は、 ぐらぐら して いた にゅうし が やっと ぬけて よろこんで いる。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother is happy that his wobbly baby tooth has finally come out.

meanings: (of teeth) to be replaced by new ones
(of fur, feathers) to moult and regrow
cards.scene: p.14 — 四葉's baby teeth haven't all been replaced by adult ones yet.
cards.context: 生える (to grow — of teeth, hair, plants) + 替わる (to be replaced). Usually written 生え変わる. Used for children's teeth and for animals' fur or feathers changing with the season. The book says 全部生え替わってない, dropping the い of 〜ていない as people do in speech.
cards.example_sentence: うちの犬は、春になると毛が生え替わって、部屋中が毛だらけになる。
cards.example_reading: うち の いぬ は、 はる に なる と け が はえかわって、 へやじゅう が けだらけ に なる。
cards.example_meaning: Every spring our dog's coat comes in anew, and the whole room ends up covered in fur.

cards.scene: p.14 — 四葉 has apparently decided, once and for all, that she's the reliable sister.
cards.context: Also 断ずる (more formal). 〜と断じる = to declare flatly that…, pass a firm verdict. The book has 断じている節がある — 節がある means 'there are signs that / she seems to'. Don't confuse with the adverb 断じて (absolutely not: 断じて許さない).
cards.example_sentence: その記事は、事故の原因を運転手の不注意だと断じていた。
cards.example_reading: その きじ は、 じこ の げんいん を うんてんしゅ の ふちゅうい だ と だんじて いた。
cards.example_meaning: The article flatly concluded that the accident was caused by the driver's carelessness.

cards.scene: p.14 — Instead of saying sorry, 三葉 just promises to cook tomorrow: no apologising to her little sister.
cards.context: 謝罪する = to apologise formally — companies and politicians do it (謝罪会見 = a press conference of apology). Using such a stiff word for a breakfast squabble is the joke. Everyday versions: 謝る (あやまる), ごめん.
cards.example_sentence: 社長は記者会見で、客に正式に謝罪した。
cards.example_reading: しゃちょう は きしゃ かいけん で、 きゃく に せいしき に しゃざい した。
cards.example_meaning: The company president formally apologised to customers at a press conference.

cards.scene: p.14 — 三葉 pops open the rice cooker to help herself to breakfast.
cards.context: 炊 (たく, to cook rice) + 飯 (はん, rice, meal) + 器 (device). Rice is 炊く, not 煮る or 作る: ご飯を炊く. The book gives the lid a sound effect, かぱん, as it springs open.
cards.example_sentence: 朝六時に炊けるように、炊飯器のタイマーをセットした。
cards.example_reading: あさ ろくじ に たける よう に、 すいはんき の タイマー を セット した。
cards.example_meaning: I set the rice cooker's timer so the rice would be ready at six in the morning.

meanings: to serve (food) onto a plate or bowl
cards.scene: p.14 — 三葉 heaps rice into her bowl — then wonders if she's taken too much.
cards.context: 盛る (to pile up) + つける; also written 盛り付ける. It covers both serving and arranging food nicely (盛りつけがきれい = beautifully plated). Related: 盛りすぎ (too big a helping), 大盛り (large portion), よそう (to dish out rice or soup).
cards.example_sentence: 母は料理を大きな皿にきれいに盛りつけた。
cards.example_reading: はは は りょうり を おおきな さら に きれい に もりつけた。
cards.example_meaning: My mother arranged the food beautifully on a large plate.

cards.scene: p.15 — grandma watches 三葉 chewing her rice.
cards.context: ガムを噛む (chew gum), 犬に噛まれる (get bitten by a dog), 舌を噛む (bite your tongue). Slang: 噛んだ! = 'I fluffed my line!'
cards.example_sentence: よく噛んで食べなさいと、祖母によく言われた。
cards.example_reading: よく かんで たべなさい と、 そぼ に よく いわれた。
cards.example_meaning: My grandmother always told me to chew my food well.

cards.scene: p.15 — grandma's inspecting gaze.
cards.context: 視 (look) + 線 (line). 視線を感じる (feel someone's eyes on you), 視線をそらす (look away), 熱い視線 (an ardent gaze). Very common in novels to track who is looking at whom.
cards.example_sentence: 後ろから誰かの視線を感じて、振り向いた。
cards.example_reading: うしろ から だれか の しせん を かんじて、 ふりむいた。
cards.example_meaning: I felt someone's eyes on me from behind and turned around.

cards.scene: p.15 — Chewing her rice, 三葉 feels someone's gaze somewhere around her temple.
cards.context: Usually written in kana (the kanji 顳顬 is very rare). Said to come from 米噛み — the spot that moves when you chew rice — fitting, since she has a mouthful of rice. こめかみを押さえる = to press your temples (headache, frustration).
cards.example_sentence: 頭が痛くて、こめかみを指で押さえた。
cards.example_reading: あたま が いたくて、 こめかみ を ゆび で おさえた。
cards.example_meaning: My head hurt, so I pressed my temples with my fingers.

cards.scene: p.15 — 三葉 senses something — a stare — fixed on her.
cards.context: 何やら adds vagueness: 'some kind of …, I can't tell what'. なにやら視線が = there's some kind of look on me. Also adverbial: なにやら怪しい (somehow suspicious). Slightly literary or old-fashioned; in speech people say なんか or なにか.
cards.example_sentence: 隣の部屋から、なにやら楽しそうな声が聞こえてくる。
cards.example_reading: となり の へや から、 なにやら たのしそうな こえ が きこえて くる。
cards.example_meaning: Some kind of cheerful voices are coming from the next room.

cards.scene: p.15 — Grandmother looks 三葉 over as if inspecting something suspicious.
cards.context: 検分する = to inspect closely, originally an official on-site check (実地検分). The book likens grandma's stare to examining 怪しげなもの (something dubious) — the bureaucratic word makes it comic. More common relatives: 検査 (test), 点検 (check-up).
cards.example_sentence: 祖父は、骨董品を一つ一つ手に取って検分した。
cards.example_reading: そふ は、 こっとうひん を ひとつ ひとつ て に とって けんぶん した。
cards.example_meaning: My grandfather picked up each antique and examined it carefully.

cards.scene: p.15 — Without warning, the speaker blares out at full volume.
cards.context: A written, more dramatic version of 突然. Used as an adverb, often 突如として: 突如として現れる = to appear out of nowhere. 如 is rare in everyday words.
cards.example_sentence: 静かだった森の中で、突如として雷が鳴った。
cards.example_reading: しずか だった もり の なか で、 とつじょ と して かみなり が なった。
cards.example_meaning: In the quiet forest, thunder suddenly crashed.

cards.scene: p.15 — The town speaker is mounted on the lintel above the living-room doors (it goes silent there on p.16).
cards.context: The upper beam with grooves that sliding doors (襖, 障子) run in. Its partner on the floor is the 敷居 (しきい) — idiom 敷居が高い = to feel awkward about visiting someone. 鴨 means duck; just learn the reading.
cards.example_sentence: 背の高い父は、鴨居に頭をぶつけないように気をつけている。
cards.example_reading: せ の たかい ちち は、 かもい に あたま を ぶつけない よう に き を つけて いる。
cards.example_meaning: My tall father is careful not to bang his head on the door lintel.

cards.scene: p.15 — The speaker is installed on the lintel; on p.16 we learn speakers are installed outdoors all over town too.
cards.context: 設置する = to install, set up (equipment, facilities, even committees). Passive 設置されている = has been installed, is in place — a common sign word: 防犯カメラ設置 (CCTV in operation). Everyday alternative: 取りつける.
cards.example_sentence: 駅のホームに新しいエレベーターが設置された。
cards.example_reading: えき の ホーム に あたらしい エレベーター が せっち された。
cards.example_meaning: A new lift has been installed on the station platform.

cards.scene: p.15 — サヤちん's sister works at the town hall, which is why it's her voice on the speaker.
cards.context: Formal, written: 〜勤務 = works at ~ (町役場勤務 = works at the town hall). 勤務する, 勤務先 (workplace), 勤務時間 (working hours). Verb: 勤める (つとめる, to be employed at) — compare 働く (to work, labour).
cards.example_sentence: 姉は駅前の病院に勤務している。
cards.example_reading: あね は えきまえ の びょういん に きんむ して いる。
cards.example_meaning: My sister works at the hospital in front of the station.

cards.scene: p.16 — the disaster-broadcast system that doubles as the town's daily announcer.
cards.context: 防災 (disaster prevention) + 無線 (wireless, radio). Many Japanese towns have outdoor loudspeakers that play a chime every evening and carry warnings; the full name is 防災行政無線. Related: 防災訓練 (disaster drill), 防災グッズ (emergency kit).
cards.example_sentence: 毎日夕方五時になると、防災無線から音楽が流れる。
cards.example_reading: まいにち ゆうがた ごじ に なる と、 ぼうさいむせん から おんがく が ながれる。
cards.example_meaning: Every day at five in the evening, music plays from the emergency loudspeakers.

cards.scene: pp.16–17 — the mayoral election (町長選挙); 三葉's father is the mayor.
cards.context: 町 (town) + 長 (head). Compare 市長 (city mayor), 村長 (village head), 社長 (company president). Fun clash: ちょうちょう is also 蝶々 (butterfly).
cards.example_sentence: 新しい町長は、駅前の再開発を約束した。
cards.example_reading: あたらしい ちょうちょう は、 えきまえ の さいかいはつ を やくそく した。
cards.example_meaning: The new mayor promised to redevelop the area in front of the station.

cards.scene: pp.16–17 — the mayoral election on the 20th of next month.
cards.context: 選 (choose) + 挙 (raise up). 選挙運動 = election campaign; 選挙カー = a campaign van blasting a candidate's name from loudspeakers, a very Japanese sight; 立候補 (りっこうほ) = to run for office.
cards.example_sentence: 町長選挙が近づき、町中にポスターが貼られた。
cards.example_reading: ちょうちょうせんきょ が ちかづき、 まちじゅう に ポスター が はられた。
cards.example_meaning: With the mayoral election coming up, posters went up all over town.

cards.scene: p.16 — the speaker falls silent when grandma pulls the plug.
cards.context: 沈 (sink) + 黙 (be silent). Written and literary; everyday speech uses 黙る (だまる). 沈黙が続く, 沈黙を破る (break the silence). It pairs naturally with 気まずい.
cards.example_sentence: 長い沈黙を破ったのは、彼女のほうだった。
cards.example_reading: ながい ちんもく を やぶった の は、 かのじょ の ほう だった。
cards.example_meaning: It was she who broke the long silence.

cards.scene: p.16 — 三葉 calls 糸守 a shabby little town of just 1,500 people.
cards.context: Slangy and dismissive: しょぼい店 (crummy shop), しょぼい給料 (measly pay). Always kana. 三葉's frustration with her small town shows in word choices like this. Related: しょぼん (dejected), しょんぼり (downcast).
cards.example_sentence: 楽しみにしていた花火大会は、思ったよりしょぼかった。
cards.example_reading: たのしみ に して いた はなび たいかい は、 おもった より しょぼかった。
cards.example_meaning: The fireworks show I'd been looking forward to was more pathetic than I expected.

cards.scene: p.16 — The announcer reads very slowly, pausing phrase by phrase.
cards.context: In Japanese school grammar a 文節 is the smallest natural chunk of speech — a word plus any particles stuck to it, the place where you could slip in ね: わたしは(ね)きのう(ね)ほんを(ね)よんだ. 文節を区切って = pausing between those chunks, the way PA announcements are read so they carry across a valley.
cards.example_sentence: 日本の中学校では、文を文節に分ける練習をする。
cards.example_reading: にほん の ちゅうがっこう で は、 ぶん を ぶんせつ に わける れんしゅう を する。
cards.example_meaning: In Japanese middle schools, students practise dividing sentences into phrase units.

cards.scene: p.16 — The announcement is read with a pause between every phrase.
cards.context: 区 (section) + 切る (cut). 言葉を区切って話す = to speak with pauses between words; 線で区切る = to divide with a line. Noun: 区切り = a break, a milestone (区切りがいい = a good place to stop).
cards.example_sentence: 先生は大事なところを一語ずつ区切って、ゆっくり話した。
cards.example_reading: せんせい は だいじな ところ を いちご ずつ くぎって、 ゆっくり はなした。
cards.example_meaning: At the important parts, the teacher spoke slowly, pausing after each word.

cards.scene: p.16 — The broadcast echoes off the mountains all around the town.
cards.context: 反響する = to echo, reverberate: 声が山に反響する. Figurative and very common in the news: 大きな反響を呼ぶ = to cause a big response or stir. 響 (ひびく, resound) is also in 影響 (influence).
cards.example_sentence: トンネルの中では、自分の足音が大きく反響した。
cards.example_reading: トンネル の なか で は、 じぶん の あしおと が おおきく はんきょう した。
cards.example_meaning: Inside the tunnel, my own footsteps echoed loudly.

cards.scene: p.16 — The echoes overlap across the valley like a round.
cards.context: 輪 (ring) + 唱 (sing): a song where each group starts the same tune a little later, like 'Row, Row, Row Your Boat'. Japanese schoolchildren sing かえるの歌 as a 輪唱. A lovely image for the same announcement arriving a beat late from each distant speaker.
cards.example_sentence: 音楽の時間に、クラスを三つに分けて輪唱をした。
cards.example_reading: おんがく の じかん に、 クラス を みっつ に わけて りんしょう を した。
cards.example_meaning: In music class we split into three groups and sang a round.

cards.scene: p.16 — The town broadcast goes out twice a day, morning and evening, without fail.
cards.context: Kanji 欠かさず: 欠かす (to miss, go without) + the classical negative ず; the book writes it in kana. Typical: 毎日欠かさず (every single day). Related: 欠かせない = indispensable (水は生活に欠かせない).
cards.example_sentence: 祖父は毎朝かかさず散歩に出かける。
cards.example_reading: そふ は まいあさ かかさず さんぽ に でかける。
cards.example_meaning: My grandfather goes for a walk every morning without fail.

cards.scene: p.16 — Every house in town has a receiver for the disaster-warning broadcasts.
cards.context: 受信 (receiving a signal) + 器 (device); more often written 受信機. Opposite: 送信 (sending). Many rural Japanese homes have an indoor receiver for the 防災無線 (disaster-prevention radio) — that's the speaker on 三葉's lintel.
cards.example_sentence: 山の上では電波が弱く、受信器がうまく働かない。
cards.example_reading: やま の うえ で は でんぱ が よわく、 じゅしんき が うまく はたらかない。
cards.example_meaning: On top of the mountain the signal is weak, so the receiver doesn't work well.

cards.scene: p.16 — Day after day, the broadcast dutifully announces every little town event, births and funerals included.
cards.context: Read りちぎ — 律 is normally りつ, so drill it. Describes someone who keeps promises and does things properly, sometimes almost too faithfully: 律儀な人, 律儀にお礼を言う. Also spelled 律義. The narration treats the speaker like a diligent little helper.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は律儀な人で、借りた本は必ず期限までに返す。
cards.example_reading: かれ は りちぎな ひと で、 かりた ほん は かならず きげん まで に かえす。
cards.example_meaning: He's a conscientious person — he always returns borrowed books by the due date.

cards.scene: p.16 — The speaker itself is mounted too high for grandmother to reach.
cards.context: The main body of a machine, as opposed to its cord, remote or accessories: パソコン本体, スピーカー本体. On price tags, 本体価格 = price before tax. Can also mean the true form of something.
cards.example_sentence: ケースは傷だらけだが、本体は無事だった。
cards.example_reading: ケース は きず だらけ だ が、 ほんたい は ぶじ だった。
cards.example_meaning: The case is all scratched up, but the phone itself was fine.

cards.scene: p.16 — Grandmother, past eighty, is always dressed in elegant, old-style 着物.
cards.context: 古式 (ancient custom or style) + ゆかしい (refined, quietly charming; 床しい). A set phrase for ceremonies and festivals: 古式ゆかしい儀式. Using it for grandma's everyday 着物 gently highlights her dignified, traditional ways.
cards.example_sentence: その神社では、毎年古式ゆかしい祭りが行われる。
cards.example_reading: その じんじゃ で は、 まいとし こしきゆかしい まつり が おこなわれる。
cards.example_meaning: A time-honoured festival is held at that shrine every year.

cards.scene: p.16 — Grandmother shows her anger without saying a word.
cards.context: 無 (without) + 言 (words). 無言で = silently; 無言のまま = staying silent; 無言電話 = a silent (prank) phone call. 黙る (だまる) is the everyday verb. The family tension around the election comes across through this silence.
cards.example_sentence: 父は怒ると、無言で部屋を出ていく。
cards.example_reading: ちち は おこる と、 むごん で へや を でて いく。
cards.example_meaning: When my father gets angry, he leaves the room without a word.

cards.scene: p.16 — Grandmother makes her anger known silently, by pulling the plug.
cards.context: 表明する = to state or declare formally: 意見を表明する, 立候補を表明する (announce one's candidacy). A political news word — wry when used for grandma's silent protest, especially since the broadcast was about an election.
cards.example_sentence: その歌手は、引退を表明した。
cards.example_reading: その かしゅ は、 いんたい を ひょうめい した。
cards.example_meaning: The singer announced her retirement.

cards.scene: p.17 — TV news: the once-in-1,200-years comet is a month away.
cards.context: 彗 (broom — a comet looks like a sweeping broom) + 星. Compare 流れ星 (shooting star), 隕石 (meteorite), 惑星 (planet). The comet is the story's ticking clock — expect it in every chapter.
cards.example_sentence: 千年に一度の彗星を見るために、多くの人が山に登った。
cards.example_reading: せんねん に いちど の すいせい を みる ため に、 おおく の ひと が やま に のぼった。
cards.example_meaning: Lots of people climbed the mountain to see the once-in-a-thousand-years comet.

cards.scene: p.17 — the comet will be visible to the naked eye for days.
cards.context: 肉 (flesh) + 眼 (eye). 肉眼で見える = visible to the naked eye. Opposite: 望遠鏡 (ぼうえんきょう, telescope).
cards.example_sentence: 今夜は、肉眼でも土星が見えるらしい。
cards.example_reading: こんや は、 にくがん で も どせい が みえる らしい。
cards.example_meaning: Apparently you can see Saturn with the naked eye tonight.

cards.scene: p.17 — blurry footage of the comet on TV.
cards.context: 写真がぼやける (a photo is blurry), 視界がぼやける (your vision blurs, e.g. through tears), 記憶がぼやける. Similar: かすむ.
cards.example_sentence: 涙で、前がぼやけて見えない。
cards.example_reading: なみだ で、 まえ が ぼやけて みえない。
cards.example_meaning: My eyes are blurred with tears and I can't see ahead.

cards.scene: p.17 — the conversation trails off.
cards.context: 途 (way, route) + 切れる (be cut): something continuous stopping partway. 話が途切れる (the conversation dies), 記憶が途切れる (memory has gaps), 電波が途切れる. Contrast 途絶える (とだえる): stopping and staying stopped.
cards.example_sentence: トンネルに入ると、ラジオの音が途切れた。
cards.example_reading: トンネル に はいる と、 ラジオ の おと が とぎれた。
cards.example_meaning: When we entered the tunnel, the radio cut out.

cards.scene: p.17 — down the narrow road along the slope.
cards.context: 斜 (slant, diagonal) + 面 (surface). 斜面 is a natural slope or hillside; 坂 is usually a road or path that goes up or down. 急な斜面 = a steep slope. The same 斜 is in 斜め (ななめ, diagonal).
cards.example_sentence: 雨のあとの斜面は滑りやすいので気をつけて。
cards.example_reading: あめ の あと の しゃめん は すべりやすい ので き を つけて。
cards.example_meaning: Slopes are slippery after rain, so be careful.

cards.scene: p.17 — The NHK newsreader announces that the comet's visit, which comes only once every 1,200 years, is now a month away.
cards.context: 来 (come) + 訪 (visit, as in 訪問 ほうもん and 訪れる おとずれる). Formal news and written register: the broadcast talks about the comet as if an honoured guest were arriving (彗星の来訪). In speech you'd say 来る or 訪れる; 来訪者 (visitor) is common on office signs.
cards.example_sentence: 町長の来訪に合わせて、学校は朝から大掃除をした。
cards.example_reading: ちょうちょう の らいほう に あわせて、 がっこう は あさ から おおそうじ を した。
cards.example_meaning: The school did a big clean-up from the morning in time for the mayor's visit.

cards.scene: p.17 — The comet should be observable with the naked eye for several days, and institutions worldwide are preparing their observations.
cards.context: Scientific observation, often with instruments: 天体観測 (astronomical observation, stargazing), 気象観測 (weather observation), 観測史上初 (a first in recorded history). Don't mix it up with 観察 (かんさつ), close watching, e.g. insects in science class. 肉眼でも観測できる = visible even to the naked eye.
cards.example_sentence: 今夜は晴れるので、屋上で星の観測をしよう。
cards.example_reading: こんや は はれる ので、 おくじょう で ほし の かんそく を しよう。
cards.example_meaning: It'll be clear tonight, so let's watch the stars from the roof.

cards.scene: p.17 — TV hype for the comet: 天体ショー, a celestial show, and the biggest one of the century.
cards.context: 天 (sky, heaven) + 体 (body): stars, planets, moons and comets are all 天体. 天体観測 = stargazing; 天体望遠鏡 = astronomical telescope. 天体ショー is a media phrase for eclipses, meteor showers and comets.
cards.example_sentence: 子どものころ、父と天体望遠鏡で月を見た。
cards.example_reading: こども の ころ、 ちち と てんたいぼうえんきょう で つき を みた。
cards.example_meaning: When I was little, I looked at the moon with my dad through a telescope.

cards.scene: p.17 — With the sky show of the century close at hand (〜を目前に), research bodies are getting ready.
cards.context: The written-register form of 目の前 (めのまえ), right in front of you in space or time. 〜を目前に(して) = 'with ~ just ahead': 試験を目前に, 卒業を目前にして. 目前に迫る = to be imminent. Note 目 is read もく here, as in 目的 and 目標.
cards.example_sentence: 卒業を目前にして、急に寂しくなった。
cards.example_reading: そつぎょう を もくぜん に して、 きゅうに さびしく なった。
cards.example_meaning: With graduation just around the corner, I suddenly felt lonely.

cards.scene: p.17 — Research institutions around the world, JAXA among them, are busy preparing to observe the comet.
cards.context: 研究 (research) + 機関 (organisation, body; also 'engine' as in 蒸気機関, steam engine). 機関 shows up in formal names: 交通機関 (public transport), 報道機関 (the news media), 金融機関 (financial institutions). A 研究所 (けんきゅうじょ) is one institute; 研究機関 is the general category.
cards.example_sentence: その大学は国の研究機関と協力して、新しい薬を開発している。
cards.example_reading: その だいがく は くに の けんきゅうきかん と きょうりょく して、 あたらしい くすり を かいはつ して いる。
cards.example_meaning: The university is working with a national research institution to develop a new medicine.

cards.scene: p.17 — The institutions are said to be busy with their preparations (準備に追われる) for observing the comet.
cards.context: The passive of 追う (to chase), so literally 'to be chased'. With に it means being kept running by something: 仕事に追われる, 時間に追われる, 準備に追われる. It says 'busy' with more pressure than 忙しい.
cards.example_sentence: 母は毎朝、家事と仕事の準備に追われている。
cards.example_reading: はは は まいあさ、 かじ と しごと の じゅんび に おわれて いる。
cards.example_meaning: Every morning my mother is swamped with housework and getting ready for work.

cards.scene: p.17 — The eating sounds are like a secret talk whispered during class (授業中の密談みたい).
cards.context: 密 (secret, dense, as in 秘密 ひみつ) + 談 (talk, as in 相談 and 会談). 密談 is normally adult and a bit shady, like politicians making backroom deals. 三葉 uses it for schoolkids whispering, which makes fun of the awkward silence at breakfast.
cards.example_sentence: 二人は教室の隅で、何やら密談をしている。
cards.example_reading: ふたり は きょうしつ の すみ で、 なにやら みつだん を して いる。
cards.example_meaning: The two of them are having some kind of secret talk in the corner of the classroom.

cards.scene: p.17 — The eating noises sound strangely guilty (book: 後ろめたげ), as if nobody should be making a sound.
cards.context: A nagging guilty feeling, as if someone behind you knows what you did. The book uses 後ろめたげ: adjective stem + げ = 'seeming ~' (as in 寂しげ, 楽しげ), so 'guilty-sounding'. 罪悪感 (ざいあくかん, sense of guilt) is the stronger, more formal word.
cards.example_sentence: 友達の宿題を写してしまって、少し後ろめたい。
cards.example_reading: ともだち の しゅくだい を うつして しまって、 すこし うしろめたい。
cards.example_meaning: I copied my friend's homework, so I feel a bit guilty.

cards.scene: p.17 — Just after 三葉 snaps at 四葉, a kite somewhere gives a goofy-sounding cry (間抜けな音色).
cards.context: 間 (ま, timing, rhythm) + 抜け (missing): originally 'off the beat', now 'dim-witted' or 'goofy'. As a noun it's an insult (この間抜け！ = you idiot!), but as a な-adjective it often just means comically silly: 間抜けな顔, 間抜けな声. Here the kite's cry breaks the tension.
cards.example_sentence: 寝起きの兄は、間抜けな顔であくびをした。
cards.example_reading: ねおき の あに は、 まぬけな かお で あくび を した。
cards.example_meaning: My brother, just out of bed, yawned with a goofy look on his face.

cards.scene: p.17 — The kite's cry has a goofy tone to it.
cards.context: 音 read ね (as in 本音 ほんね) + 色 (colour): the 'colour' of a sound, its timbre. Usually for instruments and pleasant sounds: ピアノの音色, 美しい音色 (sometimes read おんしょく in technical use). Using it for a bird's silly cry is gently comic.
cards.example_sentence: 古いオルゴールから、やさしい音色が流れてきた。
cards.example_reading: ふるい オルゴール から、 やさしい ねいろ が ながれて きた。
cards.example_meaning: A gentle tone came from the old music box.

cards.scene: p.17 — Somewhere a black kite cries ぴーひょろろ, the classic sound of the Japanese countryside.
cards.context: Kanji 鳶 (read とび or とんび); written トンビ in katakana as an animal name. Its cry is written ぴーひょろろ (ピーヒョロロ). Proverb: 鳶が鷹を生む (とびがたかをうむ), 'a kite gives birth to a hawk', meaning ordinary parents with a brilliant child.
cards.example_sentence: 海の上の空を、トンビがゆっくり回っている。
cards.example_reading: うみ の うえ の そら を、 トンビ が ゆっくり まわって いる。
cards.example_meaning: A kite is circling slowly in the sky above the sea.

cards.scene: p.17 — Outside, the summer mountain birds are singing at full volume (盛大に).
cards.context: Normally describes grand events: 盛大なパーティー, 盛大な拍手 (thunderous applause). As an adverb, 盛大に means 'in a big way' and is often used jokingly for things that aren't grand at all, such as 盛大に転ぶ (to take a spectacular fall). Here the birds are singing for all they're worth.
cards.example_sentence: 卒業式のあと、盛大な拍手が起こった。
cards.example_reading: そつぎょうしき の あと、 せいだいな はくしゅ が おこった。
cards.example_meaning: After the graduation ceremony, there was thunderous applause.

cards.scene: p.17 — The sisters go down a narrow road along the slope and several sets of stone-wall steps.
cards.context: 石 (stone) + 垣 (かき, fence; がき after the sound change): walls of piled stones that support castles and hold up terraced slopes in mountain villages. 生垣 (いけがき) = a hedge. 石垣の階段 = steps built into a stone retaining wall.
cards.example_sentence: お城の石垣は、四百年以上前に積まれたものだ。
cards.example_reading: おしろ の いしがき は、 よんひゃくねん いじょう まえ に つまれた もの だ。
cards.example_meaning: The castle's stone walls were piled up more than 400 years ago.

cards.scene: p.18 — direct sunlight pours down on them.
cards.context: The book writes it 降りそそぐ (kanji 降り注ぐ). 降る + 注ぐ: rain, sunlight, stars or even praise pouring down — 日差しが降り注ぐ, 降り注ぐ星. Gentler and more poetic than 落ちる.
cards.example_sentence: 窓から明るい日差しが降り注いでいた。
cards.example_reading: まど から あかるい ひざし が ふりそそいで いた。
cards.example_meaning: Bright sunlight was pouring in through the window.

cards.scene: p.18 — the calm lake shines brazenly in the sun.
cards.context: Stronger and more beautiful than 光る — brilliant, radiant light. Figurative too: 目が輝く (eyes light up), 輝かしい未来 (a brilliant future). Noun: 輝き.
cards.example_sentence: 雨上がりの夜空に、星が輝いていた。
cards.example_reading: あめあがり の よぞら に、 ほし が かがやいて いた。
cards.example_meaning: Stars were shining in the night sky after the rain.

cards.scene: p.18 — 'in short, we live in the Showa-style Japanese back country' (ど田舎).
cards.context: Irregular reading (熟字訓): 田 + 舎 → いなか. Can sound negative (田舎くさい = countrified) or warm (田舎に帰る = go back to one's hometown). The country-vs-Tokyo contrast drives the early chapters.
cards.example_sentence: 田舎の夜は、星がよく見えて静かだ。
cards.example_reading: いなか の よる は、 ほし が よく みえて しずか だ。
cards.example_meaning: Nights in the countryside are quiet, and you can see the stars well.

cards.scene: p.18 — テッシー grumpily pedalling his bike (自転車を漕ぐ).
cards.context: Covers any repeated pushing motion: 自転車を漕ぐ, ボートを漕ぐ, ブランコを漕ぐ. 立ち漕ぎ = pedalling standing up (for steep hills). Fun idiom: 舟を漕ぐ = to nod off, head bobbing like rowing.
cards.example_sentence: 坂道で立ち上がって、思いきりペダルを漕いだ。
cards.example_reading: さかみち で たちあがって、 おもいきり ペダル を こいだ。
cards.example_meaning: On the slope I stood up and pedalled as hard as I could.

cards.scene: p.18 — Out of the mountain's shadow, direct sunlight pours down on the sisters.
cards.context: 直射 (shining straight down; 直 + 射る いる, to shoot) + 日光 (sunlight). You'll know it from labels: 直射日光を避けて保存してください (store out of direct sunlight). Often paired with 降りそそぐ / 降り注ぐ (to pour down).
cards.example_sentence: この薬は直射日光の当たらない場所に置いてください。
cards.example_reading: この くすり は ちょくしゃにっこう の あたらない ばしょ に おいて ください。
cards.example_meaning: Please keep this medicine somewhere out of direct sunlight.

cards.scene: p.18 — From the slope, the round lake, 糸守湖, lies spread out below.
cards.context: 眼 (eye, がん as in 肉眼 and 眼科) + 下: the view down from a height. 眼下に広がる = to spread out below. Descriptive written style; in speech you'd say 下に見える. Not the same as 目の下 (under your eyes, as with dark circles).
cards.example_sentence: 山の上から、眼下に町の明かりが広がっていた。
cards.example_reading: やま の うえ から、 がんか に まち の あかり が ひろがって いた。
cards.example_meaning: From the top of the mountain, the town lights spread out below us.

cards.scene: p.18 — The lake's surface lies calm and still (凪いだ水面) in the windless morning.
cards.context: 凪 (なぎ) is a lull: no wind and a mirror-flat sea or lake. The verb 凪ぐ usually appears as 凪いだ (calm) before a noun. 朝凪 (あさなぎ) / 夕凪 (ゆうなぎ) = the morning/evening calm. 凪 is a kanji made in Japan: 止 (stop) inside 几 (from 風, wind).
cards.example_sentence: 風がやんで、海はすっかり凪いでいた。
cards.example_reading: かぜ が やんで、 うみ は すっかり ないで いた。
cards.example_meaning: The wind had stopped, and the sea was completely calm.

cards.scene: p.18 — The lake glitters with no restraint at all (ぴかーっと無遠慮に), dazzlingly bright.
cards.context: 無 read ぶ (as in 無事 ぶじ and 無礼 ぶれい) + 遠慮 (holding back, politeness). Of people it's negative: rude or presumptuous (無遠慮な質問). Of light it's personification: the lake shines without caring about your eyes, a typical 新海 touch.
cards.example_sentence: 初対面なのに、彼は無遠慮に私の年齢を聞いてきた。
cards.example_reading: しょたいめん なのに、 かれ は ぶえんりょ に わたし の ねんれい を きいて きた。
cards.example_meaning: Even though we'd only just met, he bluntly asked my age.

meanings: to be linked in a row
cards.scene: p.18 — Deep-green mountains stretch in a chain (深緑に連なった山々) around the lake.
cards.context: To extend in a row or chain: 山々が連なる (a mountain range), 屋根が連なる (rows of roofs). The transitive form is 連ねる (つらねる, to line up), as in 名を連ねる. Same kanji as 連続 (れんぞく, continuous).
cards.example_sentence: 窓の外には、雪をかぶった山が連なっている。
cards.example_reading: まど の そと に は、 ゆき を かぶった やま が つらなって いる。
cards.example_meaning: Outside the window, snow-capped mountains stretch in a line.

cards.scene: p.18 — Beside 三葉, 四葉 skips along innocently with her red school backpack.
cards.context: 無 (none) + 邪気 (malice, ill will): without any bad intentions, like a child. 無邪気な笑顔 = an innocent smile. Said of an adult it can be mildly critical (naive). 純粋 (じゅんすい, pure) is close but is more about sincerity.
cards.example_sentence: 公園で遊ぶ子どもたちの無邪気な笑い声が聞こえる。
cards.example_reading: こうえん で あそぶ こどもたち の むじゃきな わらいごえ が きこえる。
cards.example_meaning: I can hear the carefree laughter of children playing in the park.

cards.scene: p.18 — 三葉 imagines grand string music (壮大なストリングス) playing over the view, like the opening of a film.
cards.context: 壮 (strong, magnificent) + 大: on a vast, impressive scale. 壮大な景色, 壮大な計画, 壮大な音楽. Compare 盛大 (せいだい), grand in the sense of lively or lavish events; 壮大 is about majesty and scale.
cards.example_sentence: 飛行機の窓から、壮大な富士山の姿が見えた。
cards.example_reading: ひこうき の まど から、 そうだいな ふじさん の すがた が みえた。
cards.example_meaning: From the plane window I could see the majestic shape of Mount Fuji.

cards.scene: p.18 — サヤちん is perched on the rear rack of テッシー's bicycle.
cards.context: 荷 (load, as in 荷物) + 台 (stand, platform): the part of a bike, motorbike or truck where cargo goes. 自転車の荷台 = a bike's rear rack; トラックの荷台 = a truck bed. Two people on one bike (二人乗り) is actually against the traffic rules in Japan.
cards.example_sentence: 自転車の荷台に箱をしばって運んだ。
cards.example_reading: じてんしゃ の にだい に はこ を しばって はこんだ。
cards.example_meaning: I tied a box onto my bike's rack and carried it.

cards.scene: p.18 — テッシー and サヤちん bicker like a married comedy double act (夫婦漫才のような…).
cards.context: 夫婦 is normally ふうふ, but the old reading めおと survives in set words: 夫婦漫才, 夫婦茶碗 (めおとぢゃわん, a his-and-hers pair of rice bowls). 漫才 (まんざい) is two-person stand-up comedy with a funny man (ボケ) and a straight man (ツッコミ). Calling a pair's bickering 夫婦漫才 hints that they're secretly a perfect match.
cards.example_sentence: あの二人の会話は、まるで夫婦漫才みたいで面白い。
cards.example_reading: あの ふたり の かいわ は、 まるで めおとまんざい みたい で おもしろい。
cards.example_meaning: Those two talk like a married comedy act. It's hilarious.

cards.scene: p.18 — 三葉 calls the pair's morning bickering a kind of flirting that they act out from first thing.
cards.context: A slangy, jokey variant of いちゃいちゃ (couples being touchy-feely and flirty), also used as イチャコラする. It usually describes public displays of affection that annoy everyone else. Using it for an argument is 三葉's joke: to her, their quarrel looks like flirting.
cards.example_sentence: 電車の中でイチャコラするカップルに、周りの人はあきれていた。
cards.example_reading: でんしゃ の なか で イチャコラ する カップル に、 まわり の ひと は あきれて いた。
cards.example_meaning: The people around them were fed up with the couple being lovey-dovey on the train.

meanings: to carry on, stage (a battle, a show)
cards.scene: p.18 — The two have been putting on their bickering act since first thing in the morning.
cards.context: To roll out something long and showy in front of others: 熱戦を繰り広げる (to put up a fierce fight), 議論を繰り広げる (to carry on a debate). Typical of news and narration. 繰る (to reel in, to turn pages) + 広げる (to spread out).
cards.example_sentence: 決勝戦では、両チームが激しい戦いを繰り広げた。
cards.example_reading: けっしょうせん で は、 りょう チーム が はげしい たたかい を くりひろげた。
cards.example_meaning: In the final, the two teams fought a fierce battle.

cards.scene: p.18 — When 三葉 says they get along well, the two deny it in perfect unison.
cards.context: Slang verb from ハーモニー (harmony) + る, conjugated as a godan verb: ハモった, ハモって. Literally to sing in harmony; jokingly, two people blurting out the same words at once. Other verbs built the same way: サボる (to skip class), メモる (to jot down).
cards.example_sentence: 二人の答えが同時にハモって、みんな笑った。
cards.example_reading: ふたり の こたえ が どうじ に ハモって、 みんな わらった。
cards.example_meaning: The two of them answered in unison, and everyone laughed.

cards.scene: p.18 — The soundtrack in 三葉's head switches to an upbeat guitar solo.
cards.context: 軽 (light) + 快 (pleasant, as in 快適): light and lively. 軽快な音楽 (upbeat music), 軽快な足取り (a spring in one's step), 軽快に走る. Watch the homophone 警戒 (けいかい, caution, alertness), which means something completely different.
cards.example_sentence: 朝のラジオから軽快な音楽が流れている。
cards.example_reading: あさ の ラジオ から けいかいな おんがく が ながれて いる。
cards.example_meaning: Upbeat music is playing on the morning radio.

cards.scene: p.18 — 三葉's 'in-head soundtrack' (私の脳内BGM) changes track as the mood shifts.
cards.context: Literally 'inside the brain' (脳内出血 = bleeding in the brain), but casual modern Japanese uses 脳内〜 to mean 'in my imagination': 脳内再生 (replaying something in your head), 脳内会議 (arguing with yourself). The everyday phrase is 頭の中.
cards.example_sentence: あの歌がずっと脳内で流れていて、勉強に集中できない。
cards.example_reading: あの うた が ずっと のうない で ながれて いて、 べんきょう に しゅうちゅう できない。
cards.example_meaning: That song keeps playing in my head, and I can't concentrate on studying.

cards.scene: p.18 — 三葉's imaginary background music switches from strings to a guitar solo.
cards.context: Intransitive 切り替わる (something switches) vs transitive 切り替える (you switch it): 画面が切り替わる (the screen changes), 気持ちを切り替える (to put something behind you and reset). Don't confuse it with 入れ替わる (two things swap places), a key word later in this chapter.
cards.example_sentence: 信号が青に切り替わると、人々は一斉に歩き出した。
cards.example_reading: しんごう が あお に きりかわる と、 ひとびと は いっせい に あるきだした。
cards.example_meaning: When the light switched to green, everyone started walking at once.

cards.scene: p.19 — サヤちん: テッシー turns everything into the occult.
cards.context: From English 'occult', but in Japanese it covers ghosts, UFOs, prophecies and ancient mysteries — the whole mystery-magazine world. オカルト好き, オカルトマニア. The formal word is 超常現象 (ちょうじょうげんしょう, paranormal phenomena).
cards.example_sentence: 兄はオカルト雑誌を毎月欠かさず買っている。
cards.example_reading: あに は オカルト ざっし を まいつき かかさず かって いる。
cards.example_meaning: My older brother buys an occult magazine every single month.

cards.scene: p.19 — テッシー is lanky and tall (ひょろりとした長身).
cards.context: A written word for a tall person: 長身の男性, 長身でやせている. In speech, 背が高い. Its written opposite is 小柄 (こがら, small-built). ひょろりとした = lanky, thin and tall.
cards.example_sentence: 新しいコーチは、長身でやさしそうな人だった。
cards.example_reading: あたらしい コーチ は、 ちょうしん で やさしそうな ひと だった。
cards.example_meaning: The new coach was a tall, kind-looking man.

cards.scene: p.19 — テッシー has a shaven head, which 三葉 thinks is a bit uncool.
cards.context: A 坊主 (ぼうず) is a Buddhist monk, who shaves his head, so 坊主頭 = a buzz cut. It's traditional for boys on school baseball teams; 坊主にする = to shave your head. 坊主 can also mean 'little boy' (affectionate), and a 三日坊主 is someone who gives up after three days.
cards.example_sentence: 野球部に入った弟は、坊主頭にして帰ってきた。
cards.example_reading: やきゅうぶ に はいった おとうと は、 ぼうずあたま に して かえって きた。
cards.example_meaning: My brother joined the baseball team and came home with his head shaved.

cards.scene: p.19 — テッシー and サヤちん always seem to be squabbling.
cards.context: From いがむ (to snarl, like dogs baring their teeth) + 合う (each other): two people constantly hostile or bickering. Stronger and more ongoing than けんかする, though here it's softened by ふう ('they seem to'). Typical pattern: いつもいがみ合っている.
cards.example_sentence: あの兄弟は小さいころからいがみ合ってばかりだ。
cards.example_reading: あの きょうだい は ちいさい ころ から いがみあって ばかり だ。
cards.example_meaning: Those brothers have done nothing but squabble since they were small.

cards.scene: p.19 — 三葉 secretly thinks テッシー and サヤちん would make a good couple.
cards.context: Secretly, without others knowing, often about feelings or plans: 密かに思う, 密かに好きだった. More literary than こっそり, which suits sneaky physical actions (こっそり食べる). Same kanji as 秘密 and 密談; also written 秘かに.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は密かに、留学の準備を進めていた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は ひそかに、 りゅうがく の じゅんび を すすめて いた。
cards.example_meaning: She was secretly preparing to study abroad.

cards.scene: p.19 — サヤちん, off the bike now, touches 三葉's hair cord and grins.
cards.context: 髪 (hair) + 紐 (ひも, cord, string). 三葉's hair cord is a braided 組紐 (くみひも), the traditional craft of her family's shrine, and a red cord that matters a great deal in this story. An ordinary elastic hair tie is a 髪ゴム or ヘアゴム.
cards.example_sentence: 祖母が編んでくれた髪紐で、髪を一つに結んだ。
cards.example_reading: そぼ が あんで くれた かみひも で、 かみ を ひとつ に むすんだ。
cards.example_meaning: I tied my hair back with the hair cord my grandmother braided for me.

cards.scene: p.19 — The coiled braids are gathered and tied together behind her head with the cord (髪紐で束ねる).
cards.context: 束 (たば, a bundle; 花束 はなたば = bouquet) → 束ねる = to bind things into one bundle: 髪を束ねる (to tie back your hair), 新聞を束ねる. Figuratively, to lead or unite a group: チームを束ねる.
cards.example_sentence: 古い新聞をひもで束ねて、玄関の前に出した。
cards.example_reading: ふるい しんぶん を ひも で たばねて、 げんかん の まえ に だした。
cards.example_meaning: I tied the old newspapers into a bundle with string and put them out by the front door.

cards.scene: p.19 — The talk at breakfast about her strange behaviour the day before was left unresolved.
cards.context: Left vague, never given a clear answer: 話がうやむやになる, 問題をうやむやにする (to fudge or hush up an issue). Rarely written 有耶無耶 ('is it there or isn't it?'). Close to あいまい, but うやむや stresses that the matter was never settled.
cards.example_sentence: 誰が窓を割ったのか、結局うやむやになってしまった。
cards.example_reading: だれ が まど を わった の か、 けっきょく うやむや に なって しまった。
cards.example_meaning: In the end, who broke the window was never cleared up.

meanings: to set out on, launch into
cards.scene: p.19 — テッシー leans in with a worried face (心配顔を乗りだした).
cards.context: Two senses: (1) physical: 身を乗り出す = to lean forward out of interest or concern; 窓から身を乗り出す = to lean out of a window; (2) to embark on something: 調査に乗り出す (to launch an investigation). The book writes 乗りだす with だす in kana.
cards.example_sentence: おもしろい話になると、弟は身を乗り出して聞いた。
cards.example_reading: おもしろい はなし に なる と、 おとうと は み を のりだして きいた。
cards.example_meaning: When the story got interesting, my brother leaned forward to listen.

cards.scene: p.19 — テッシー asks whether 三葉's grandmother gave her a proper purification after the day before.
cards.context: 祓う (はらう) = to drive away impurity or evil by ritual; お祓い is the Shinto rite, done by a priest waving a paper-streamer wand (大幣 おおぬさ). 三葉's family runs the local shrine, so テッシー half-seriously suggests it. Same sound as 払う (to pay, brush off), different kanji.
cards.example_sentence: 新しい車を買ったので、神社でお祓いをしてもらった。
cards.example_reading: あたらしい くるま を かった ので、 じんじゃ で おはらい を して もらった。
cards.example_meaning: I bought a new car, so I had it purified at the shrine.

cards.scene: p.19 — テッシー, the occult fan, declares that 三葉's behaviour was definitely fox possession (in dialect: 狐憑きやぜ).
cards.context: 狐 (きつね, fox) + 憑き (from 憑く つく, to possess, haunt): an old folk belief that a fox spirit can take over a person and make them act strangely. 憑く is a different kanji from 付く (to attach). テッシー loves the occult (オカルト), and サヤちん teases him for it.
cards.example_sentence: 昔の村では、急に様子がおかしくなった人を狐憑きだと言うことがあった。
cards.example_reading: むかし の むら で は、 きゅうに ようす が おかしく なった ひと を きつねつき だ と いう こと が あった。
cards.example_meaning: In old villages, people who suddenly began acting strangely were sometimes said to be possessed by a fox.

cards.scene: p.19 — At テッシー's sudden fox-possession theory, 三葉 grimaces.
cards.context: しかめる (rare kanji 顰める) = to scrunch up your face in displeasure or pain: 顔をしかめる, 眉をしかめる (to knit your brows). しかめっ面 (しかめっつら) = a scowl. Compare にらむ (to glare at someone).
cards.example_sentence: 薬が苦くて、子どもは顔をしかめた。
cards.example_reading: くすり が にがくて、 こども は かお を しかめた。
cards.example_meaning: The medicine was bitter, and the child made a face.

cards.scene: p.19 — Exasperated with テッシー, サヤちん speaks up for 三葉: she's just stressed.
cards.context: 代 (in place of) + 弁 (speech, as in 弁論 and 関西弁): to say what someone else thinks or feels on their behalf. 気持ちを代弁する = to put someone's feelings into words for them; 代弁者 = spokesperson. Watch out for 大便 (だいべん, feces), which sounds exactly the same.
cards.example_sentence: 私の言いたいことを、友達が全部代弁してくれた。
cards.example_reading: わたし の いいたい こと を、 ともだち が ぜんぶ だいべん して くれた。
cards.example_meaning: My friend said everything I wanted to say, for me.

cards.scene: p.20 — her father's mayoral campaign speech.
cards.context: 演説する = to make a speech, especially a political one. 街頭演説 (がいとうえんぜつ) = street-corner speech. スピーチ is the lighter word (weddings, school).
cards.example_sentence: 駅前で候補者が演説をしていた。
cards.example_reading: えきまえ で こうほしゃ が えんぜつ を して いた。
cards.example_meaning: A candidate was making a speech in front of the station.

cards.scene: p.20 — A voice booming through a megaphone breaks into 三葉's thoughts: a campaign speech in the town car park.
cards.context: 拡 (expand) + 声 (voice) + 器 (device) = 'voice-enlarging device'. Covers handheld megaphones and the speakers on election vans (選挙カー). Same 拡 as 拡大 (enlargement). Everyday speech often just says マイク or メガホン.
cards.example_sentence: 選挙カーが拡声器で候補者の名前を何度も叫んでいる。
cards.example_reading: せんきょ カー が かくせいき で こうほしゃ の なまえ を なんど も さけんで いる。
cards.example_meaning: An election van keeps shouting the candidate's name through its loudspeaker.

cards.scene: p.20 — The megaphone voice is thick and gruff, a man's voice that drowns out 三葉's wondering.
cards.context: Almost always 野太い声: a deep, coarse, rough-edged (usually male) voice. 野 (wild, rustic) adds roughness to 太い (thick); 太い声 is merely deep. Not a compliment; it hints at something unrefined or overbearing. Reading の, not や.
cards.example_sentence: 後ろの席から野太い笑い声が聞こえてきた。
cards.example_reading: うしろ の せき から のぶとい わらいごえ が きこえて きた。
cards.example_meaning: A deep, booming laugh came from the seats behind us.

cards.scene: p.20 — The megaphone voice wipes out 三葉's question, and she never gets back to puzzling over yesterday.
cards.context: 消す (erase) + 去る (go away) = erase so that nothing is left. Used for memories, fears, traces, doubts: 記憶を消し去る, 不安を消し去る. Written, literary feel. A quiet hint, too: memories being wiped away runs through the whole book.
cards.example_sentence: 楽しい音楽が、その日の嫌な気分を消し去ってくれた。
cards.example_reading: たのしい おんがく が、 その ひ の いやな きぶん を けしさって くれた。
cards.example_meaning: Cheerful music wiped away that day's bad mood.

cards.scene: p.20 — Across from a row of plastic greenhouses lies the town car park where the crowd has gathered.
cards.context: 立ち並ぶ is the general spelling (trees, people, shops); 建ち並ぶ is used for buildings and structures (建 = build). Typically 〜が建ち並ぶ + place: ビルが建ち並ぶ大通り. ビニールハウス = a plastic (vinyl) greenhouse, a standard sight in rural Japan.
cards.example_sentence: 駅前には新しいマンションが建ち並んでいる。
cards.example_reading: えきまえ に は あたらしい マンション が たちならんで いる。
cards.example_meaning: New apartment blocks line the area in front of the station.

cards.scene: p.20 — On the car park's wide, empty grounds, a little crowd has gathered.
cards.context: The plot of land belonging to a building or facility: 学校の敷地 (school grounds), 敷地内禁煙 (no smoking on the premises). 敷 = spread, lay (敷く しく, as in 布団を敷く) + 地 = ground. 土地 is land in general.
cards.example_sentence: 学校の敷地の中では自転車に乗ってはいけない。
cards.example_reading: がっこう の しきち の なか で は じてんしゃ に のって は いけない。
cards.example_meaning: You're not allowed to ride bikes on the school grounds.

cards.scene: p.20 — A crowd of about a dozen people (a crowd by 糸守 standards) has formed around the speaker.
cards.context: 人だかりができる = a crowd forms, as people stop to look at something. From 人 + たかる (to swarm, like flies). Different from 人込み / 人混み (ひとごみ), a crowded place you push through. 一ダース = a dozen: twelve people counting as a crowd is part of the gentle humour.
cards.example_sentence: 駅前に人だかりができていて、何かと思ったら有名な歌手だった。
cards.example_reading: えきまえ に ひとだかり が できて いて、 なにか と おもったら ゆうめいな かしゅ だった。
cards.example_meaning: A crowd had formed in front of the station; I wondered what was going on, and it turned out to be a famous singer.

cards.scene: p.20 — 三葉's father stands out from the crowd: noticeably taller than everyone and imposing.
cards.context: Kanji 一際. Standing out from everything around it: ひときわ背が高い (taller than all the others), ひときわ目立つ, ひときわ明るい星. Written, slightly literary; close to いちだんと or 特に.
cards.example_sentence: 夜空の中で、その星だけがひときわ明るく光っていた。
cards.example_reading: よぞら の なか で、 その ほし だけ が ひときわ あかるく ひかって いた。
cards.example_meaning: In the night sky, that one star shone conspicuously bright.

cards.scene: p.20 — Over his suit, her father wears an election sash that proudly reads 「現職」 with his name.
cards.context: Kanji 襷. Japanese election candidates wear a white sash with their name; relay runners (駅伝) pass on a たすき instead of a baton, so たすきをつなぐ = to pass the torch. Originally a cord for tying back kimono sleeves.
cards.example_sentence: 駅伝では、選手がたすきを次の走者に渡す。
cards.example_reading: えきでん で は、 せんしゅ が たすき を つぎ の そうしゃ に わたす。
cards.example_meaning: In a long-distance relay, each runner hands the sash to the next.

cards.scene: p.20 — The sash reads 「現職」: her father is the sitting mayor, running for re-election.
cards.context: 現 (present) + 職 (job, post). In elections 現職 = the incumbent, as opposed to 新人 (しんじん, a newcomer) and 元職 (もとしょく, a former holder). Also 現職の警察官 = a serving police officer. Printing 現職 on the sash advertises experience, and power.
cards.example_sentence: 今回の市長選挙では、現職が三回目の当選を目指している。
cards.example_reading: こんかい の しちょう せんきょ で は、 げんしょく が さんかいめ の とうせん を めざして いる。
cards.example_meaning: In this mayoral election, the incumbent is aiming to win a third time.

cards.scene: p.21 — he 'renews his resolve' (決意を新たに).
cards.context: 決意する, 決意を固める (firm up one's resolve). Weightier than 決める; close to 決心, but 決意 sounds more formal and steely.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は一人で山へ向かう決意をした。
cards.example_reading: かれ は ひとり で やま へ むかう けつい を した。
cards.example_meaning: He resolved to head into the mountains alone.

cards.scene: p.21 — the crowd assumes he'll win again this term.
cards.context: 再 (again) + 選 (elect). 再選を目指す = to aim for re-election. 当選 = winning an election; 落選 = losing.
cards.example_sentence: 市長は三期目の再選を果たした。
cards.example_reading: しちょう は さんきめ の さいせん を はたした。
cards.example_meaning: The mayor won re-election for a third term.

cards.scene: p.21 — In his speech her father promises to put the town's finances on a sound footing.
cards.context: The money side of a government or organisation: 町の財政, 財政難 (financial trouble), 財政赤字 (budget deficit). 財政健全化 (けんぜんか) = making finances sound, a stock campaign phrase. 財 = wealth (as in 財布 さいふ), 政 = government (政治).
cards.example_sentence: 町の財政が厳しくて、図書館が閉まることになった。
cards.example_reading: まち の ざいせい が きびしくて、 としょかん が しまる こと に なった。
cards.example_meaning: The town's finances are so tight that the library is going to close.

cards.scene: p.21 — The mayor promises further development for the town, in stiff speech-making language.
cards.context: Kanji 更なる. Only before a noun: さらなる発展 (further development), さらなる努力, さらなる問題. The adverb is さらに (furthermore, even more). Formal, written register: the language of politicians and company statements.
cards.example_sentence: 優勝したチームは、さらなる成長を目指して練習を続けている。
cards.example_reading: ゆうしょう した チーム は、 さらなる せいちょう を めざして れんしゅう を つづけて いる。
cards.example_meaning: The winning team keeps practising, aiming for further growth.

cards.scene: p.21 — Her father vows to lead the town with fresh passion: big words for a car-park speech.
cards.context: 情 (feeling) + 熱 (heat). 情熱を注ぐ (to pour passion into), 情熱的 (passionate). Stronger and more emotional than やる気; in a campaign speech it sounds grand. 新たな情熱で = with renewed passion.
cards.example_sentence: 祖父は九十歳になった今も、陶芸に情熱を注いでいる。
cards.example_reading: そふ は きゅうじゅっさい に なった いま も、 とうげい に じょうねつ を そそいで いる。
cards.example_meaning: Even now at ninety, my grandfather pours his passion into pottery.

cards.scene: p.21 — 'I will lead this land': the mayor reaches for the lofty verb 導く.
cards.context: To lead people or a place somewhere: 町を導く, 勝利に導く (lead to victory), 生徒を導く. Loftier than 案内する (show the way). この地 (this land) is equally grand: formal, almost old-fashioned oratory. 導 (guide) as in 指導 (しどう, coaching).
cards.example_sentence: キャプテンの言葉が、チームを勝利に導いた。
cards.example_reading: キャプテン の ことば が、 チーム を しょうり に みちびいた。
cards.example_meaning: The captain's words led the team to victory.

cards.scene: p.21 — 'That is my mission,' her father declares, and even he slips into the local や for だ.
cards.context: A duty you feel called to, heavier than 役目 or 仕事: 使命を果たす (fulfil one's mission), 使命感 (sense of mission). In the book he says 使命や, the 糸守 copula や (= だ), even in a formal speech.
cards.example_sentence: 医者としての使命は、一人でも多くの命を救うことだ。
cards.example_reading: いしゃ として の しめい は、 ひとり でも おおく の いのち を すくう こと だ。
cards.example_meaning: A doctor's mission is to save as many lives as possible.

cards.scene: p.21 — 三葉 finds her father's speech almost overbearing, like a politician on TV, not a man in a car park next to the fields.
cards.context: 高圧 = high pressure (also high voltage: 高圧線) + 的. 高圧的な態度 / 言い方 = pushy, talking down to people. 高圧的なほど = to the point of being overbearing. Casual near-synonyms: 偉そう, いばっている.
cards.example_sentence: あの先輩は高圧的な言い方をするので、後輩に嫌われている。
cards.example_reading: あの せんぱい は こうあつてきな いいかた を する ので、 こうはい に きらわれて いる。
cards.example_meaning: That senior talks down to people, so the juniors dislike him.

cards.scene: p.21 — Her father's speech is slick and well-rehearsed; he has clearly done this many times.
cards.context: Read どうにいる, not はいる: the old reading of 入る survives in set phrases (気に入る きにいる, 恐れ入る). Usually 堂に入った + noun: 堂に入った演説 (a polished speech), 堂に入った演技. From Confucius: having 'entered the hall' = reached mastery. Positive on its own; next to 高圧的 it sounds smugly rehearsed.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は初めての司会とは思えないほど堂に入っていた。
cards.example_reading: かれ は はじめて の しかい と は おもえない ほど どう に いって いた。
cards.example_meaning: He was so polished you'd never guess it was his first time as host.

cards.scene: p.21 — Watching her father's grand speech among the fields, 三葉 feels cold and turned off (白々とした気持ち).
cards.context: Read しらじら here, not はくはく. 白々とした気持ち = a flat, sobered, 'this is embarrassing' feeling, related to しらける (the mood dies, you're put off). Don't confuse with 白々しい (しらじらしい, transparently false: 白々しい嘘). Also 夜が白々と明ける = dawn breaks pale.
cards.example_sentence: 大人たちの作り笑いを見て、なんだか白々とした気分になった。
cards.example_reading: おとなたち の つくりわらい を みて、 なんだか しらじら と した きぶん に なった。
cards.example_meaning: Seeing the adults' fake smiles, I felt oddly cold and let down.

cards.scene: p.21 — 'It'll be 宮水 again this term': the listeners treat the election as a done deal.
cards.context: Read こんき (今 = こん as in 今月, 今週). 期 = a term or period: 任期 (term of office), 前期 / 後期 (first / second half), 今期の売上 (this term's sales). 今期も = this term too, implying he has won before.
cards.example_sentence: この会社は今期、過去最高の利益を出した。
cards.example_reading: この かいしゃ は こんき、 かこ さいこう の りえき を だした。
cards.example_meaning: This company posted record profits this term.

cards.scene: p.21 — Townsfolk whisper that he has been spreading plenty around: slang for handing out money to buy votes.
cards.context: Literally to scatter or sprinkle: 水を撒く, 豆を撒く (seeds: 種を蒔く). Said of money, (お金を)撒く / ばらまく means handing it out freely; in an election it hints at vote-buying. The book's だいぶ撒いてる has no object; listeners fill in 'money'. Usually written in kana: まく.
cards.example_sentence: 暑い日には、店の前に水を撒いて涼しくする。
cards.example_reading: あつい ひ に は、 みせ の まえ に みず を まいて すずしく する。
cards.example_meaning: On hot days they sprinkle water in front of the shop to cool it down.

cards.scene: p.21 — Cynical whispers drift from the small audience listening to the speech.
cards.context: 聴 (listen closely) + 衆 (crowd, as in 大衆, 民衆). For people listening to speeches, lectures and concerts; 観客 (かんきゃく) is spectators at sport or a play; 視聴者 (しちょうしゃ) is TV viewers.
cards.example_sentence: 彼の演奏が終わると、聴衆は立ち上がって拍手した。
cards.example_reading: かれ の えんそう が おわる と、 ちょうしゅう は たちあがって はくしゅ した。
cards.example_meaning: When his performance ended, the audience rose to applaud.

cards.scene: p.21 — Whispered remarks among the listeners make 三葉's mood sink even lower.
cards.context: 囁く (ささやく, to whisper) + 声 (こえ → ごえ, the same sound change as 笑い声 わらいごえ). The rare kanji 囁 is 口 + three 耳: a mouth at the ears. Often written in kana: ささやき. Also used of rumours spreading quietly.
cards.example_sentence: 図書館の奥から、誰かの囁き声が聞こえてきた。
cards.example_reading: としょかん の おく から、 だれか の ささやきごえ が きこえて きた。
cards.example_meaning: Someone's whispering came from the back of the library.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 三葉's father doesn't live with the family.
cards.context: 別 (separate) + 居 (live). 同居 (どうきょ) = living together. 別居 is living apart, not divorce (離婚).
cards.example_sentence: 両親は仕事の都合で別居している。
cards.example_reading: りょうしん は しごと の つごう で べっきょ して いる。
cards.example_meaning: My parents live apart because of work.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): テッシー's family runs the local construction company — a big deal in a small town.
cards.context: 土木 (civil engineering) + 建築 (building) + 屋 (trade/shop). Slightly blunt and colloquial; the neutral term is 建設会社 (けんせつがいしゃ). In small towns the builder and the town office are often closely tied.
cards.example_sentence: 叔父は田舎で小さな土建屋をやっている。
cards.example_reading: おじ は いなか で ちいさな どけんや を やって いる。
cards.example_meaning: My uncle runs a small construction firm out in the countryside.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 三葉 has to put up with classmates sniping about her family behind her back.
cards.context: 陰 (shadow) + 口 (mouth). 陰口を言う / 陰口をたたく = to badmouth someone behind their back. 悪口 (わるぐち) is any insult; 陰口 is specifically said where the person can't hear — or is meant to overhear.
cards.example_sentence: 陰口を言う人とは、あまり付き合いたくない。
cards.example_reading: かげぐち を いう ひと と は、 あまり つきあいたくない。
cards.example_meaning: I don't really want to hang around people who talk behind others' backs.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 三葉's classical-literature class, where the teacher explains old words for twilight.
cards.context: At Japanese high schools 古典 means classical Japanese and Chinese texts (古文 + 漢文). Also 'a classic' in general: 古典的 = classic(al). This one lesson plants several of the book's key words.
cards.example_sentence: 古典の授業で、千年以上前の和歌を読んだ。
cards.example_reading: こてん の じゅぎょう で、 せんねん いじょう まえ の わか を よんだ。
cards.example_meaning: In classical literature class we read poems from over a thousand years ago.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The teacher explains old words for twilight.
cards.context: 古 (old) + 語 (word). 誰そ彼 is a 古語. Opposite: 現代語 (げんだいご, modern language).
cards.example_sentence: 古語の意味は、辞書で調べないと分からない。
cards.example_reading: こご の いみ は、 じしょ で しらべない と わからない。
cards.example_meaning: You can't understand archaic words without looking them up.

meanings: the Man'yōshū (oldest anthology of Japanese poetry)
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The teacher's example of the old word for twilight comes from a 万葉集 poem.
cards.context: About 4,500 poems compiled in the 8th century. 万 (ten thousand) + 葉 (leaves = words) + 集 (collection). Notice 葉 — the same kanji as in 三葉 and 四葉.
cards.example_sentence: 万葉集には、身分を問わずさまざまな人の歌が収められている。
cards.example_reading: まんようしゅう に は、 みぶん を とわず さまざまな ひと の うた が おさめられて いる。
