cards.example_meaning: The Man'yōshū contains poems by all kinds of people, regardless of rank.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The teacher's example comes from an old poem.
cards.context: 和 (Japanese) + 歌 (song, poem). 5-7-5-7-7 syllables; today it's usually called 短歌 (たんか). 俳句 is 5-7-5.
cards.example_sentence: 和歌は五・七・五・七・七の三十一音でできている。
cards.example_reading: わか は ご・しち・ご・しち・しち の さんじゅういち おん で できて いる。
cards.example_meaning: A waka is made of thirty-one syllables: five, seven, five, seven, seven.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The twilight lesson in class: dusk is when you can't quite make out who someone is.
cards.context: 黄昏 (たそがれ) is a 熟字訓 — a special reading of the whole word that you can't get from the separate kanji. It comes from 誰そ彼 ('who is that?'). Also figurative: 人生の黄昏 (the twilight of life). Twilight matters enormously later.
cards.example_sentence: 黄昏時の空は、オレンジから紫へと色を変えた。
cards.example_reading: たそがれどき の そら は、 オレンジ から むらさき へ と いろ を かえた。
cards.example_meaning: The twilight sky changed from orange to purple.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): At twilight, people's outlines blur so you can't tell who they are.
cards.context: 輪 (ring) + 郭 (enclosure). 顔の輪郭 = the shape of a face; 輪郭がぼやける = an outline blurs.
cards.example_sentence: 霧の中で、山の輪郭がかすんで見えた。
cards.example_reading: きり の なか で、 やま の りんかく が かすんで みえた。
cards.example_meaning: In the fog, the outline of the mountain looked hazy.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The teacher writes this old phrase to show where the word for twilight comes from.
cards.context: Classical Japanese: 誰 (た, who) + そ (emphatic particle, like modern ぞ) + 彼 (かれ, that person) → 'Who is that?' At dusk you can't tell faces apart, so you have to ask. It later softened into たそがれ.
cards.example_sentence: 「誰そ彼」は、夕暮れに人の顔が見えにくいことから生まれた言葉だ。
cards.example_reading: 「たそかれ」 は、 ゆうぐれ に ひと の かお が みえにくい こと から うまれた ことば だ。
cards.example_meaning: 'Tasokare' is a word born from how hard it is to see people's faces at dusk.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The lesson traces たそがれ back to its origin.
cards.context: 語 (word) + 源 (source). 〜の語源は… = the word ~ comes from ….
cards.example_sentence: 「ありがとう」の語源は「有り難い」だそうだ。
cards.example_reading: 「ありがとう」 の ごげん は 「ありがたい」 だ そう だ。
cards.example_meaning: Apparently 'arigatō' comes from 'arigatai'.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The classical twin of 誰そ彼 — worth knowing next to the twilight words from 三葉's class.
cards.context: 彼 (か, that) + は + 誰 (たれ, who) → 'Who is that?' — the same question, asked at dawn. Classical poets used かはたれ for morning twilight and たそかれ for evening.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は誰時の薄暗い道を、新聞配達の自転車が走っていく。
cards.example_reading: かはたれどき の うすぐらい みち を、 しんぶんはいたつ の じてんしゃ が はしって いく。
cards.example_meaning: A newspaper delivery bike rides down the dim road in the half-light before dawn.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Root of the town's own word for twilight (かたわれ時) — and a word the whole story leans on.
cards.context: 片 (one side) + 割れ (split). Three senses, and the book plays on all of them: one of a matched pair (a lost glove's 片割れ), a fragment of something broken, and someone's 'other half'.
cards.example_sentence: 片方の手袋をなくして、残った片割れだけが引き出しにある。
cards.example_reading: かたほう の てぶくろ を なくして、 のこった かたわれ だけ が ひきだし に ある。
cards.example_meaning: I lost one glove, and only its partner is left in the drawer.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): In class it comes up that in Itomori's local speech, twilight is called かたわれ時.
cards.context: The town's own word for dusk, from 片割れ (one half of a pair) + 時. A hint that at twilight, two halves might meet. Remember it — it matters a great deal later in the book.
cards.example_sentence: かたわれ時になると、湖の色が少しずつ変わっていく。
cards.example_reading: かたわれどき に なる と、 みずうみ の いろ が すこし ずつ かわって いく。
cards.example_meaning: At twilight, the colour of the lake gradually changes.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): With no café in town, 三葉 and her friends hang out on a bench by a vending machine instead.
cards.context: Short for 自動販売機 (じどうはんばいき, 'automatic selling machine'). Japan has one on almost every corner — even deep in the countryside.
cards.example_sentence: 駅前の自販機で、温かいお茶を買った。
cards.example_reading: えきまえ の じはんき で、 あたたかい おちゃ を かった。
cards.example_meaning: I bought hot tea from the vending machine in front of the station.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Itomori is a small town deep in the mountains.
cards.context: 山 + 奥 (the inner part). 山奥の村 = a remote mountain village.
cards.example_sentence: 祖父は山奥の小さな村で育った。
cards.example_reading: そふ は やまおく の ちいさな むら で そだった。
cards.example_meaning: My grandfather grew up in a small village deep in the mountains.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): A small town where everyone knows your family feels stifling to 三葉.
cards.context: Physically tight (この靴は窮屈だ) or socially constraining (窮屈な生活).
cards.example_sentence: 小さな町では、みんなに見られているようで窮屈だ。
cards.example_reading: ちいさな まち で は、 みんな に みられて いる よう で きゅうくつ だ。
cards.example_meaning: In a small town it feels stifling, as if everyone is watching you.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 三葉, 四葉 and their grandmother make braided cords by hand — a family tradition of the shrine.
cards.context: 組む (to braid, put together) + 紐 (ひも, cord/string). Made on a wooden braiding stand. 三葉 ties her hair with one. Arguably the most important object in the story — notice every time it appears.
cards.example_sentence: おばあちゃんに習って、初めて組紐を編んだ。
cards.example_reading: おばあちゃん に ならって、 はじめて くみひも を あんだ。
cards.example_meaning: I learned from my grandma and braided a cord for the first time.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Braiding the cords with grandmother.
cards.context: セーターを編む (knit a sweater), 髪を編む (braid hair → 三つ編み みつあみ = a braid), 本を編む (edit/compile a book). Noun: 編み物 (あみもの, knitting).
cards.example_sentence: 冬になると、母は毎年マフラーを編んでくれた。
cards.example_reading: ふゆ に なる と、 はは は まいとし マフラー を あんで くれた。
cards.example_meaning: Every winter, my mother would knit me a scarf.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The braiding and the rituals are handed down from grandmother to the sisters.
cards.context: 受ける + 継ぐ. 伝統を受け継ぐ, 父の店を受け継ぐ. Similar: 引き継ぐ (to take over a job or task).
cards.example_sentence: 祖父の技術を、父が受け継いだ。
cards.example_reading: そふ の ぎじゅつ を、 ちち が うけついだ。
cards.example_meaning: My father inherited my grandfather's skills.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Grandmother tells of a great fire long ago that burned the town's old records — so the meaning of the rituals was lost and only their form remains.
cards.context: Read たいか, not おおび. Old town fires are often named after where they started (〜の大火). 火事 (かじ) is the everyday word for a house fire.
cards.example_sentence: 江戸時代の大火で、町の半分が焼けてしまった。
cards.example_reading: えどじだい の たいか で、 まち の はんぶん が やけて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: Half the town burned down in a great fire during the Edo period.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Grandmother keeps the shrine's customs even though their meaning has been lost.
cards.context: Usually written in kana (仕来り). The unwritten rules of a family or place: 家のしきたり, 昔からのしきたり. 伝統 is bigger and prouder.
cards.example_sentence: 祖母の家には、正月の細かいしきたりがある。
cards.example_reading: そぼ の いえ に は、 しょうがつ の こまかい しきたり が ある。
cards.example_meaning: My grandmother's house has all sorts of little New Year customs.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The shrine's autumn festival — the night of the ritual dance — is a harvest festival.
cards.context: 豊 (abundant) + 穣 (ripe grain). 豊穣祭 = harvest festival; 五穀豊穣 (ごこくほうじょう) = 'a rich harvest of the five grains', a standard prayer at shrines. Everyday word: 豊作 (ほうさく).
cards.example_sentence: 村の人々は、神社で五穀豊穣を祈った。
cards.example_reading: むら の ひとびと は、 じんじゃ で ごこくほうじょう を いのった。
cards.example_meaning: The villagers prayed at the shrine for a bountiful harvest.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The gate marking the shrine's sacred ground, where the festival takes place.
cards.context: Passing through a 鳥居 means entering the god's space. 鳥 (bird) + 居 (to be/stay) — a 'bird perch'. 鳥居をくぐる = to pass under a torii.
cards.example_sentence: 赤い鳥居をくぐると、空気が変わった気がした。
cards.example_reading: あかい とりい を くぐる と、 くうき が かわった き が した。
cards.example_meaning: When I passed under the red torii, the air seemed to change.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The shrine grounds during the festival.
cards.context: Tricky reading: 内 is だい here (not ない). Means everything inside the shrine's boundary. 境内で遊ぶ = to play on the shrine grounds.
cards.example_sentence: 夏祭りの日、神社の境内には屋台が並んだ。
cards.example_reading: なつまつり の ひ、 じんじゃ の けいだい に は やたい が ならんだ。
cards.example_meaning: On the day of the summer festival, food stalls lined the shrine grounds.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The festival night's ritual: the dance and the sake-making.
cards.context: 儀 (ceremony) + 式 (form). 儀式を行う = to hold a ritual. Compare 〜式 (結婚式, 卒業式) and 祭り (a festival, with fun).
cards.example_sentence: 村では、春に古い儀式が行われる。
cards.example_reading: むら で は、 はる に ふるい ぎしき が おこなわれる。
cards.example_meaning: An old ritual is held in the village every spring.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 三葉 and 四葉 serve as shrine maidens at their family's shrine.
cards.context: Special reading — the kanji 巫 (フ) and 女 (ジョ) won't get you みこ. 巫女さん dance in rituals, help the priest and sell charms. White top, red hakama.
cards.example_sentence: 正月になると、神社の巫女さんたちはとても忙しい。
cards.example_reading: しょうがつ に なる と、 じんじゃ の みこ さん たち は とても いそがしい。
cards.example_meaning: At New Year, the shrine maidens are extremely busy.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The sisters perform a ritual dance at the festival in front of the townspeople.
cards.context: 舞 is slow, graceful, often sacred dance; verb 舞う (まう) — also 'to flutter': 花びらが舞う, 雪が舞う. 踊り (おどり) is livelier, more everyday dancing. 舞を舞う = to perform a dance.
cards.example_sentence: 祭りの夜、二人の巫女が神様のために舞を舞った。
cards.example_reading: まつり の よる、 ふたり の みこ が かみさま の ため に まい を まった。
cards.example_meaning: On the night of the festival, two shrine maidens danced for the god.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The dance and the sake are offerings dedicated to the god.
cards.context: 奉 (offer up respectfully) + 納 (deliver). 奉納する: dedicating sake, dances, plaques (絵馬) or performances to a shrine's god. 奉納の舞 = a dance offered to the god.
cards.example_sentence: 秋祭りでは、地元の子どもたちが太鼓を奉納する。
cards.example_reading: あきまつり で は、 じもと の こども たち が たいこ を ほうのう する。
cards.example_meaning: At the autumn festival, the local kids perform drumming as an offering.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): As part of the ritual, the shrine maidens chew rice and spit it into a small vessel to make sake — mortifying for 三葉 in front of her classmates.
cards.context: 口 + 噛み (chew) + 酒 (さけ → ざけ). One of the oldest ways to make sake: enzymes in saliva start the fermentation. This little vessel of sake matters hugely later on.
cards.example_sentence: 昔の日本では、口噛み酒を神様に供えていたという。
cards.example_reading: むかし の にほん で は、 くちかみざけ を かみさま に そなえて いた と いう。
cards.example_meaning: They say that in ancient Japan, mouth-chewed sake was offered to the gods.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The chewed sake goes into a small vessel to be offered.
cards.context: 器 = a bowl, dish or vessel (often fine ceramics). About people: 器が大きい = big-hearted.
cards.example_sentence: 祖母は、料理に合わせて器を選ぶ。
cards.example_reading: そぼ は、 りょうり に あわせて うつわ を えらぶ。
cards.example_meaning: My grandmother picks the dishes to match the food.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The ritual happens in full view of the town, classmates included.
cards.context: 人目を気にする = to worry about being seen; 人目につく = to be conspicuous. Not 一目 (ひとめ, a glance).
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は人目を気にせず、駅で泣いていた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は ひとめ を きに せず、 えき で ないて いた。
cards.example_meaning: She was crying at the station, not caring who saw.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): How 口噛み酒 works: the chewed rice ferments into sake.
cards.context: 発 (start) + 酵 (ferment). 発酵する / 発酵させる. 発酵食品 = fermented foods (味噌, 納豆, 漬物).
cards.example_sentence: 納豆は、大豆を発酵させて作る。
cards.example_reading: なっとう は、 だいず を はっこう させて つくる。
cards.example_meaning: Natto is made by fermenting soybeans.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): The long stone steps of the shrine, where 三葉 lets out her frustration.
cards.context: 石 (stone) + 段 (step). Shrines often sit at the top of a long flight of 石段. 階段 is the general word for stairs.
cards.example_sentence: 神社まで、百段以上の石段を上った。
cards.example_reading: じんじゃ まで、 ひゃくだん いじょう の いしだん を のぼった。
cards.example_meaning: I climbed more than a hundred stone steps to reach the shrine.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): Fed up, 三葉 shouts a wish about who she wants to be in her next life.
cards.context: The set: 前世 (ぜんせ, past life), 現世 (げんせ, this life), 来世 (next life). 来世は〜に生まれたい = 'In my next life I want to be born as…'. Be careful what you wish for in this story.
cards.example_sentence: 来世は鳥に生まれて、自由に空を飛びたい。
cards.example_reading: らいせ は とり に うまれて、 じゆう に そら を とびたい。
cards.example_meaning: In my next life I want to be born a bird and fly freely through the sky.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): A narration staple — characters mutter to themselves all through the book.
cards.context: 呟く = to speak quietly, often to yourself. 独り言 (ひとりごと) = talking to yourself. Also used for posting on social media.
cards.example_sentence: 「もう嫌だ」と、彼は小さく呟いた。
cards.example_reading: 「もう いや だ」 と、 かれ は ちいさく つぶやいた。
cards.example_meaning: 'I've had enough,' he muttered quietly.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book (expected later in Ch.2): 三葉's wish involves becoming a handsome boy in Tokyo.
cards.context: Slang: イケてる (cool) + メン (men, and a pun on 面 'face'). Very common in everyday speech and the media. The female equivalent is often 美人 or (slangy) 美女.
cards.example_sentence: 新しく来た先生がイケメンだと、クラスで話題になった。
cards.example_reading: あたらしく きた せんせい が イケメン だ と、 クラス で わだい に なった。
cards.example_meaning: The whole class was talking about how good-looking the new teacher was.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: At breakfast おばあちゃん looks at her granddaughter as if something isn't quite right.
cards.context: Almost always 怪訝な顔をする / 怪訝そうに — a puzzled, doubtful look at someone acting out of character. Irregular reading: 怪 is usually かい, and 訝 (as in 訝しい いぶかしい) is rare. Written register.
cards.example_sentence: 急に敬語で話し始めた兄を、妹は怪訝そうに見ていた。
cards.example_reading: きゅう に けいご で はなし はじめた あに を、 いもうと は けげん そう に みて いた。
cards.example_meaning: The younger sister looked dubiously at her brother, who had suddenly started speaking politely.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: おばあちゃん seems to sense more than she says, as if she can see straight through 'Mitsuha'.
cards.context: 見 (see) + 透かす (let light through): to look right through a pretence. Usually passive: 心を見透かされる 'to have one's thoughts read'. Related 透明 (とうめい, transparent).
cards.example_sentence: 嘘をついても、母にはすぐ見透かされてしまう。
cards.example_reading: うそ を ついて も、 はは に は すぐ みすかされて しまう。
cards.example_meaning: Even if I lie, my mother sees right through me.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 瀧 has to get ready for school in someone else's body — uniform, hair, everything unfamiliar.
cards.context: 身 (body) + 支度 (preparation). Covers washing, dressing and doing your hair: 身支度を整える. 支度 alone = preparations in general (食事の支度 'getting a meal ready').
cards.example_sentence: 朝は五分で身支度を済ませて家を出る。
cards.example_reading: あさ は ごふん で みじたく を すませて いえ を でる。
cards.example_meaning: In the mornings I get ready in five minutes and leave the house.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: With nobody who knows how to tidy it, 三葉's hair stays a mess all day.
cards.context: ぼさぼさの髪 / 髪がぼさぼさだ — uncombed, untidy. Compare さらさら (silky, smooth) and ぼうぼう (overgrown — grass, beards).
cards.example_sentence: 寝坊したので、髪がぼさぼさのまま学校へ行った。
cards.example_reading: ねぼう した ので、 かみ が ぼさぼさ の まま がっこう へ いった。
cards.example_meaning: I overslept, so I went to school with my hair a mess.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The giveaway at school — each hero keeps using the wrong word for 'I'.
cards.context: 一 (one) + 人称 (grammatical person). 二人称 = second person (あなた, お前); 三人称 = third person. Japanese has many first-person words (わたし, 僕, 俺, あたし, うち), each signalling gender and attitude — see the grammar deck.
cards.example_sentence: 日本語には一人称がたくさんあって、話し手の性格が出る。
cards.example_reading: にほんご に は いちにんしょう が たくさん あって、 はなして の せいかく が でる。
cards.example_meaning: Japanese has many first-person pronouns, and they reveal the speaker's personality.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Classmates are thrown by 'Mitsuha's' rough, boyish way of talking — and 'Taki's' friends by his oddly soft one.
cards.context: 遣い comes from 遣う 'to use (with care)', with rendaku: つかい → づかい. 言葉遣いが悪い 'uses rude language'; 言葉遣いに気をつける 'mind one's language'. Same pattern: 金遣い (spending habits).
cards.example_sentence: 先生と話すときは、言葉遣いに気をつけなさい。
cards.example_reading: せんせい と はなす とき は、 ことばづかい に き を つけなさい。
cards.example_meaning: Watch your language when you talk to teachers.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 瀧 in 三葉's body sits, walks and talks with none of her usual care, and classmates find 'her' oddly crude.
cards.context: A な-adjective for someone loud, careless and unrefined: がさつな人, がさつな動作. Its traditional opposite is しとやか (graceful, ladylike) — the gap between the two is the joke of the swap.
cards.example_sentence: 兄はがさつに見えるが、実は細かいことによく気がつく。
cards.example_reading: あに は がさつ に みえる が、 じつ は こまかい こと に よく き が つく。
cards.example_meaning: My older brother seems crude, but he actually notices the little things.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Even small mannerisms give the swap away — 'Mitsuha' moves like a boy, 'Taki' like a girl.
cards.context: Small habitual movements that show who you are: かわいい仕草, 癖のある仕草. Also written 仕種. Different from ジェスチャー (deliberate signals).
cards.example_sentence: 髪を耳にかける仕草が、母にそっくりだ。
cards.example_reading: かみ を みみ に かける しぐさ が、 はは に そっくり だ。
cards.example_meaning: The way she tucks her hair behind her ear is exactly like her mother.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Classmates can't stop staring at 'Mitsuha', unable to make sense of how she's acting.
cards.context: じろじろ見る — staring openly in a way that makes the other person uncomfortable. Compare まじまじ (staring in disbelief) and ちらちら (glancing repeatedly).
cards.example_sentence: 変な服を着ていたので、電車の中でじろじろ見られた。
cards.example_reading: へん な ふく を きて いた ので、 でんしゃ の なか で じろじろ みられた。
cards.example_meaning: I was wearing weird clothes, so people stared at me on the train.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 三葉 wakes up in a boy's room in a Tokyo apartment where he lives with just his father.
cards.context: 父子 is read ふし here (not ちちこ). The counterpart is 母子家庭 (ぼしかてい, single-mother household); the neutral modern term is ひとり親家庭. 三葉's own home is also missing parents — a quiet parallel.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は父子家庭で育ったので、料理が得意だ。
cards.example_reading: かれ は ふしかてい で そだった ので、 りょうり が とくい だ。
cards.example_meaning: He grew up in a single-father household, so he's good at cooking.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Squeezed between strangers on the morning train, 三葉 can barely move.
cards.context: ぎゅうぎゅう詰め = crammed full; ぎゅうぎゅうに押し込む = cram in. A single ぎゅっと is a tight squeeze or hug. Compare すし詰め (packed like sushi).
cards.example_sentence: エレベーターは人でぎゅうぎゅうだった。
cards.example_reading: エレベーター は ひと で ぎゅうぎゅう だった。
cards.example_meaning: The elevator was jam-packed with people.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Station platforms and streets overflow with people — a sight unthinkable in her small town.
cards.context: Also written 人込み. 混む (to be crowded) with rendaku → ごみ. 人混みに紛れる 'blend into the crowd'; 人混みが苦手 'bad with crowds'.
cards.example_sentence: 人混みの中で、友達を見失ってしまった。
cards.example_reading: ひとごみ の なか で、 ともだち を みうしなって しまった。
cards.example_meaning: I lost sight of my friend in the crowd.

meanings: hustle and bustle of a crowd
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The kind of word narration uses to paint the noise and motion of Tokyo streets around 三葉.
cards.context: 雑 (mixed) + 踏 (step): countless feet treading. A literary word for a crowded, noisy place: 都会の雑踏, 雑踏に紛れる. More atmospheric than 人混み.
cards.example_sentence: 都会の雑踏の中にいると、なぜか孤独を感じる。
cards.example_reading: とかい の ざっとう の なか に いる と、 なぜか こどく を かんじる。
cards.example_meaning: In the bustle of the city, I somehow feel lonely.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Cars, trains and people stream past in every direction around 三葉.
cards.context: Also read ゆきかう (more literary). 人々が行き交う, 車が行き交う — continuous traffic both ways. Different from すれ違う, which is two people passing each other once.
cards.example_sentence: 駅前の交差点を、たくさんの人が行き交っている。
cards.example_reading: えきまえ の こうさてん を、 たくさん の ひと が いきかって いる。
cards.example_meaning: Crowds of people are coming and going across the intersection in front of the station.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 三葉 gawks at everything — trains, signs, shop windows — like the newcomer she is.
cards.context: きょろきょろする — moving your eyes and head around because you're lost, curious or nervous. Compare うろうろ (wandering about on foot) and まじまじ (fixed, disbelieving stare).
cards.example_sentence: 初めて東京に来た弟は、駅でずっときょろきょろしていた。
cards.example_reading: はじめて とうきょう に きた おとうと は、 えき で ずっと きょろきょろ して いた。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother, in Tokyo for the first time, kept looking all around at the station.

meanings: to get carried away with excitement
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Living out her dream of Tokyo, 三葉 can't contain her excitement.
cards.context: Behaving noisily and childishly because you're excited: 子供のようにはしゃぐ. Written in kana (the kanji 燥ぐ is rare). Can sound a little critical — 'getting carried away'.
cards.example_sentence: 雪を見た子供たちは、外ではしゃいでいた。
cards.example_reading: ゆき を みた こども たち は、 そと で はしゃいで いた。
cards.example_meaning: The children who saw the snow were romping around outside.

cards.simpler_synonym: すごすぎて何も言えない
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The scale and speed of Tokyo leave 三葉 overwhelmed as well as thrilled.
cards.context: 圧 (pressure) + 倒 (topple). Active 圧倒する 'to overwhelm, crush (an opponent)'; 圧倒的 'overwhelming' (圧倒的な人気). The passive is the usual way to say a sight or a person blew you away.
cards.example_sentence: 初めて海を見たとき、その大きさに圧倒された。
cards.example_reading: はじめて うみ を みた とき、 その おおきさ に あっとう された。
cards.example_meaning: When I first saw the sea, I was overwhelmed by its size.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The cafés and shops 三葉 visits after school feel impossibly stylish and grown-up.
cards.context: Usually 洗練された 'refined, polished': 洗練されたデザイン, 洗練された店. 洗 (wash) + 練 (knead, refine) — washed and worked until smooth.
cards.example_sentence: その店は小さいが、洗練された雰囲気がある。
cards.example_reading: その みせ は ちいさい が、 せんれん された ふんいき が ある。
cards.example_meaning: The shop is small, but it has a refined atmosphere.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 司 and 高木 stare open-mouthed as 'Taki' fumbles for the right word for 'I'.
cards.context: ぽかんとする / 口をぽかんと開ける — frozen with a blank face because you can't follow what's happening. Compare ぼうっと (spaced out, daydreaming).
cards.example_sentence: 突然の話に、みんなぽかんとしていた。
cards.example_reading: とつぜん の はなし に、 みんな ぽかんと して いた。
cards.example_meaning: Everyone just stared blankly at the sudden news.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Under her new friends' puzzled looks, 三葉's explanations come out in a flustered jumble.
cards.context: しどろもどろになる / しどろもどろに答える — speech falling apart because you're panicking or have been caught out. It even sounds tangled and stumbling.
cards.example_sentence: 先生に急に質問されて、しどろもどろになった。
cards.example_reading: せんせい に きゅう に しつもん されて、 しどろもどろ に なった。
cards.example_meaning: When the teacher suddenly asked me a question, I got flustered and tongue-tied.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: わたし… no, 僕… no, 俺 — 三葉 keeps correcting herself mid-sentence.
cards.context: Vます-stem + 直す = redo: 書き直す (rewrite), やり直す (start over). 言い直す is fixing what you just said: 〜と言い直した.
cards.example_sentence: 名前を間違えたので、あわてて言い直した。
cards.example_reading: なまえ を まちがえた ので、 あわてて いいなおした。
cards.example_meaning: I got the name wrong, so I hurriedly corrected myself.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Everything 'Taki' does with his friends — talking, walking, joking — comes out stiff and unnatural.
cards.context: For movements, smiles, conversations or relationships that aren't smooth: ぎこちない笑顔, 二人の間がぎこちない. It's one adjective — not a negative of some word ぎこち.
cards.example_sentence: 久しぶりに会ったので、最初は会話がぎこちなかった。
cards.example_reading: ひさしぶり に あった ので、 さいしょ は かいわ が ぎこちなかった。
cards.example_meaning: We hadn't met in ages, so the conversation was awkward at first.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The everyday slang of 瀧 and his friends at school and at work.
cards.context: Short for 真面目 (まじめ). マジで？ 'Seriously?', マジかよ 'No way!' (rough), マジでうまい 'really tasty'. Usually katakana; very casual — never with teachers or bosses.
cards.example_sentence: え、マジで？明日テストなの？
cards.example_reading: え、 マジ で？ あした テスト な の？
cards.example_meaning: Wait, seriously? There's a test tomorrow?

cards.simpler_synonym: お金をたくさん使うこと
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Fancy pancakes at a stylish café cost more than 三葉 can believe — an extravagance by her town's standards.
cards.context: な-adjective and noun: 贅沢な食事, 贅沢を言う 'to be picky, ask for too much'. Both kanji are hard; note 貝 (shell = money) at the bottom of 贅.
cards.example_sentence: たまには贅沢をして、高いレストランに行こう。
cards.example_reading: たま に は ぜいたく を して、 たかい レストラン に いこう。
cards.example_meaning: Let's treat ourselves once in a while and go to an expensive restaurant.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 三葉 gazes dreamily at the cafés, sweets and stylish people of Tokyo.
cards.context: うっとりする / うっとりと見とれる — lost in admiration of something beautiful. Compare ぼうっと (spaced out, with no admiration involved).
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は美しい夜景にうっとりしていた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は うつくしい やけい に うっとり して いた。
cards.example_meaning: She was entranced by the beautiful night view.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 三葉 has to cover 瀧's waiter shift at an Italian restaurant with no idea what she's doing.
cards.context: 接 (contact) + 客 (customer). 接客業 = the service industry; 接客態度 = attitude toward customers. A standard word in part-time-job talk.
cards.example_sentence: 接客のアルバイトで、敬語が上手になった。
cards.example_reading: せっきゃく の アルバイト で、 けいご が じょうず に なった。
cards.example_meaning: My customer-service job made me better at polite Japanese.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: A rude customer at the restaurant starts making trouble.
cards.context: False friend: Japanese クレーム means a complaint, not a 'claim'. クレームをつける 'to make a complaint'; a habitual complainer is a クレーマー. Neutral synonym: 苦情 (くじょう).
cards.example_sentence: 店員の態度にクレームをつける客がいた。
cards.example_reading: てんいん の たいど に クレーム を つける きゃく が いた。
cards.example_meaning: There was a customer complaining about a staff member's attitude.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: A customer starts hassling the staff, and the evening shift turns ugly.
cards.context: Basic sense 'to get tangled' (糸が絡む). 人に絡む = to pick on someone, often drunkenly or aggressively: 酔っ払いに絡まれた. Also 'to be involved in' (事件に絡む).
cards.example_sentence: 帰り道で、知らない男に絡まれて怖かった。
cards.example_reading: かえりみち で、 しらない おとこ に からまれて こわかった。
cards.example_meaning: On the way home, a strange man hassled me, and I was scared.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The customer slashes 奥寺先輩's skirt with a knife — the shocking moment of 三葉's shift.
cards.context: 切る (cut) + 裂く (tear). Violent and sudden: 布を切り裂く; also figurative, 静けさを切り裂く悲鳴 'a scream that tears the silence'. Related 裂ける 'to split, tear (by itself)'.
cards.example_sentence: 雷の光が、夜空を切り裂いた。
cards.example_reading: かみなり の ひかり が、 よぞら を きりさいた。
cards.example_meaning: A flash of lightning ripped across the night sky.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 奥寺先輩 is left with a tear in her skirt in the middle of her shift.
cards.context: 裂ける (to tear) + 目 (point, spot) — like 割れ目 (crack) and 切れ目 (cut, break). For clothes, 破れ目 / 破れたところ is more everyday.
cards.example_sentence: ズボンの裂け目から、ひざが見えていた。
cards.example_reading: ズボン の さけめ から、 ひざ が みえて いた。
cards.example_meaning: My knee was showing through the tear in my trousers.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Sewing is something 三葉 is good at — and in 瀧's body it saves the day at the restaurant.
cards.context: 裁 (cut cloth) + 縫 (sew). 裁縫が得意 'good at sewing'; 裁縫箱 = sewing box. 裁 also appears in 裁判 (trial) — 'cutting' a judgment.
cards.example_sentence: 祖母に教わったおかげで、裁縫が得意になった。
cards.example_reading: そぼ に おそわった おかげ で、 さいほう が とくい に なった。
cards.example_meaning: Thanks to my grandmother teaching me, I became good at sewing.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: 三葉, in 瀧's body, sews up the damaged skirt on the spot.
cards.context: 縫い目 (seam), 縫い物 (sewing work), 傷口を縫う (stitch a wound). Figurative: 人混みを縫って歩く 'weave through a crowd'. Pairs with 結う and 編む in the story's thread-and-cord vocabulary.
cards.example_sentence: とれたボタンを自分で縫いつけた。
cards.example_reading: とれた ボタン を じぶん で ぬいつけた。
cards.example_meaning: I sewed the button that had come off back on myself.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Instead of a plain repair, the tear is turned into a pretty embroidered design.
cards.context: 刺 (pierce) + 繍 (embroider). 刺繍する / 刺繍を入れる 'to embroider (a design on)'. 繍 is a rare kanji you'll basically only meet in this word — learn ししゅう as a unit.
cards.example_sentence: ハンカチに花の刺繍を入れてプレゼントした。
cards.example_reading: ハンカチ に はな の ししゅう を いれて プレゼント した。
cards.example_meaning: I embroidered flowers on a handkerchief and gave it as a present.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Everyone watches as 'Taki' fixes the skirt with surprising speed and skill.
cards.context: 手際がいい / 手際よく — doing a job quickly and neatly. 不手際 = mishandling, a blunder (common in apologies: 不手際がありました).
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は手際よく夕食の準備を済ませた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は てぎわ よく ゆうしょく の じゅんび を すませた。
cards.example_meaning: She deftly finished getting dinner ready.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Nobody expected 瀧 to be so good with a needle and thread.
cards.context: 手先が器用 'good with one's hands'. Opposite 不器用 — also used for people who are socially clumsy (不器用な性格). 器用貧乏 = jack of all trades, master of none.
cards.example_sentence: 兄は手先が器用で、何でも自分で直してしまう。
cards.example_reading: あに は てさき が きよう で、 なんでも じぶん で なおして しまう。
cards.example_meaning: My brother is good with his hands and fixes everything himself.

meanings: to see in a new light
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: After the sewing rescue, 奥寺先輩 sees the boy she works with in a new, warmer light.
cards.context: Two senses: 'check again' (答えを見直す) and 'revise one's opinion upward' (彼を見直した 'I think better of him now'). The second is what happens when someone surprises you in a good way.
cards.example_sentence: 困っている人を助ける姿を見て、彼を見直した。
cards.example_reading: こまって いる ひと を たすける すがた を みて、 かれ を みなおした。
cards.example_meaning: Seeing him help someone in trouble, I thought much better of him.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The distant, popular senior begins to relax and chat with 'Taki'.
cards.context: Lit. 'to melt / loosen'. 〜と打ち解ける; 打ち解けた雰囲気 'a relaxed atmosphere'. It's about walls coming down between people, not just getting acquainted.
cards.example_sentence: 転校生はすぐにクラスのみんなと打ち解けた。
cards.example_reading: てんこうせい は すぐ に クラス の みんな と うちとけた。
cards.example_meaning: The transfer student quickly warmed up to everyone in the class.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: A word that fits the irony of 'Taki' out-sewing everyone — he suddenly seems full of feminine skills.
cards.context: Modern slang (2000s on) for skills stereotypically called feminine: cooking, sewing, grooming, style. 女子力が高い is used playfully, even about boys. Casual, and a little old-fashioned in its assumptions.
cards.example_sentence: 毎日お弁当を作るなんて、女子力が高いね。
cards.example_reading: まいにち お べんとう を つくる なんて、 じょしりょく が たかい ね。
cards.example_meaning: You make a packed lunch every day? You're so domestic!

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Back in their own bodies, each remembers the 'dream' only in vague, fading pieces.
cards.context: 曖昧な記憶 (hazy memory), 曖昧な返事 (noncommittal answer). Both kanji have the sun radical 日 — think 'dim light'. Very common in speech and writing.
cards.example_sentence: 子供のころの記憶は、もう曖昧になっている。
cards.example_reading: こども の ころ の きおく は、 もう あいまい に なって いる。
cards.example_meaning: My childhood memories have already become hazy.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Like any dream, the details slip away soon after waking.
cards.context: 記憶が薄れる, 関心が薄れる (interest wanes), 霧が薄れる (mist thins). A gradual fading; 薄まる is more for liquids being diluted.
cards.example_sentence: 時間がたつにつれて、悲しみは少しずつ薄れていった。
cards.example_reading: じかん が たつ に つれて、 かなしみ は すこし ずつ うすれて いった。
cards.example_meaning: As time passed, the sadness gradually faded.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Each finds diary entries on their phone that they never wrote — notes left by the other.
cards.context: You know the word; in this story the 日記 is a phone diary app that becomes two strangers' message board. 日記をつける 'keep a diary'; 日記帳 = diary book; 絵日記 = picture diary.
cards.example_sentence: 寝る前に、その日のことを日記に書いている。
cards.example_reading: ねる まえ に、 その ひ の こと を にっき に かいて いる。
cards.example_meaning: Before bed, I write about the day in my diary.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Strange entries turn up in their phones and notebooks, written in someone else's style.
cards.context: From 書き込む 'to write in, fill in'. Used for notes in a book's margins, entries on a form, and posts on forums or social media (ネットの書き込み).
cards.example_sentence: 教科書に、知らない人の書き込みがあった。
cards.example_reading: きょうかしょ に、 しらない ひと の かきこみ が あった。
cards.example_meaning: There were notes by someone I didn't know written in my textbook.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The handwriting in the notebook is clearly not their own — proof that someone else was there.
cards.context: 筆 (brush) + 跡 (trace, mark). Used when identifying who wrote something: 筆跡が似ている, 筆跡鑑定 (handwriting analysis). Everyday word: 字 (彼の字はきれい).
cards.example_sentence: この手紙の筆跡は、間違いなく父のものだ。
cards.example_reading: この てがみ の ひっせき は、 まちがいなく ちち の もの だ。
cards.example_meaning: The handwriting in this letter is definitely my father's.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Words scrawled on skin or in a notebook greet them after waking, as if someone else had been using their body.
cards.context: 落 (drop) + 書き: writing 'dropped' where it doesn't belong. 壁に落書きする (graffiti), ノートの落書き (doodles). Pen marks on your own hand that you didn't make are its creepiest form.
cards.example_sentence: 弟が私のノートに落書きをした。
cards.example_reading: おとうと が わたし の ノート に らくがき を した。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother scribbled in my notebook.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Friends say you acted strangely yesterday — and you have no idea what they mean.
cards.context: Almost always 心当たりがある / ない: 'I have (no) idea who or what it could be.' A classic question from police or worried friends: 何か心当たりはない？ Verb version: 思い当たる.
cards.example_sentence: 財布をどこに置いたか、まったく心当たりがない。
cards.example_reading: さいふ を どこ に おいた か、 まったく こころあたり が ない。
cards.example_meaning: I have absolutely no idea where I put my wallet.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Finding messages you didn't write and hearing about a day you can't remember is more than a little creepy.
cards.context: 不 (not) + 気味 (feeling); 不 is read ぶ here, as in 不用心 and 不細工. Compare 気味が悪い (same meaning, more conversational) and 気味 in 風邪気味 'a bit of a cold'.
cards.example_sentence: 誰もいないはずの部屋から音がして、不気味だった。
cards.example_reading: だれ も いない はず の へや から おと が して、 ぶきみ だった。
cards.example_meaning: A sound came from a room that should have been empty — it was eerie.

meanings: to be embarrassed (in front of others)
to make a fool of oneself
cards.simpler_synonym: 恥ずかしい思いをする
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Each learns, too late, how badly 'they' embarrassed themselves while the other was in charge.
cards.context: 恥 (shame) + かく (to 'break out in', as in 汗をかく). 人前で恥をかく 'embarrass oneself in public'; 恥をかかせる 'to humiliate someone'. The shame happens to you — not something you do on purpose.
cards.example_sentence: 名前を読み間違えて、みんなの前で恥をかいた。
cards.example_reading: なまえ を よみまちがえて、 みんな の まえ で はじ を かいた。
cards.example_meaning: I misread the name and embarrassed myself in front of everyone.

cards.simpler_synonym: びっくりして落ち着かない
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Hearing about things they don't remember doing leaves both of them shaken.
cards.context: 動 (move) + 揺 (shake): the heart wobbling. 動揺する / 動揺を隠す 'hide one's agitation'. Don't confuse with 童謡 (どうよう, children's song) — same reading.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は突然の知らせに動揺して、言葉が出なかった。
cards.example_reading: かれ は とつぜん の しらせ に どうよう して、 ことば が でなかった。
cards.example_meaning: Shaken by the sudden news, he couldn't find any words.

cards.simpler_synonym: 信じていいかわからない
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Is it really just a dream? Both heroes start to wonder, only half believing the answer.
cards.context: Four-character idiom (四字熟語): 半 (half) 信 (believe) 半 疑 (doubt). 半信半疑で聞く 'listen half-believing'. Same build as 半死半生 (half dead).
cards.example_sentence: 友達の話を半信半疑で聞いていたが、本当だった。
cards.example_reading: ともだち の はなし を はんしんはんぎ で きいて いた が、 ほんとう だった。
cards.example_meaning: I listened to my friend's story half in doubt, but it turned out to be true.

cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The notes, the phone entries and the friends' reports pile up as proof the 'dream' was real.
cards.context: 証拠がある / 証拠を残す 'leave evidence'. 〜のが何よりの証拠だ 'the best proof is that…'. Related 証明 (proof in logic or maths), 保証 (guarantee).
cards.example_sentence: 彼が嘘をついているという証拠は、どこにもない。
cards.example_reading: かれ が うそ を ついて いる と いう しょうこ は、 どこ に も ない。
cards.example_meaning: There is no evidence anywhere that he is lying.

cards.simpler_synonym: きっとそうだと思うこと
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: Doubt slowly turns into certainty: this is no ordinary dream.
cards.context: 確信する / 確信を持つ / 確信に変わる 'turn into certainty'. Different from 自信 (self-confidence). Colloquially, 確信犯 = someone who does wrong knowingly.
cards.example_sentence: 彼の目を見て、彼が犯人だと確信した。
cards.example_reading: かれ の め を みて、 かれ が はんにん だ と かくしん した。
cards.example_meaning: Looking into his eyes, I was convinced he was the culprit.

meanings: to trade places with each other
cards.scene: Not yet checked against the book: The chapter's big realisation — when they sleep, the boy and the girl swap bodies.
cards.context: 入れる + 替わる: one goes in as the other comes out. Noun 入れ替わり is the story's word for the body swap. Transitive 入れ替える 'to replace, swap (something)': 空気を入れ替える 'to air out a room'.
cards.example_sentence: 席替えで、私と彼女の席が入れ替わった。
cards.example_reading: せきがえ で、 わたし と かのじょ の せき が いれかわった。
cards.example_meaning: In the seat change, she and I swapped places.
